{"assumptions":["G is finite, connected, simple, distance-regular, and n>=2."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.364496+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_07e8c48717f2e4462cbff10644f98ed2bdee48e66a11c8ccf4e48c023be5f089","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls at the two extremes.] This is the proved identity behind the campaign reduction of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). Let G be a finite connected simple distance-regular graph with n>=2 vertices, valency k, and diameter d: for vertices at distance i, the numbers of neighbors one step closer to or farther from the target are constants c_i and b_i depending only on i. For the simple random walk, let T_y be the first hitting time of y, measured in steps, and define tau_0=max_{x,y} E_x[T_y]; here tau_0 is the maximum mean hitting time, not the spectral Kemeny sum. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.364803+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08404f6e59878a825820ca327edb10eee2cc843aed665463efecc18e44df0221","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:slopestability of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A \textbf{central charge}, also known as a \textit{stability function}, on an abelian category $\cA$ is an additive map $Z\colon K_0(\cA)\to\bC$ such that $Z(E)\in\bR_{>0}e^{\sqrt{-1}(0,\pi]}$ for $0\neq E\in\cA$, i.e.\ $Z(E)$ lies in the upper half-plane or negative real axis.
The \textbf{phase} of a non-zero object $E$ is defined to be $\phi(E)=\arg(Z(E))/\pi\in(0,1]$.
An object $E\in\cA$ is said to be
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{semistable} if $0\neq A\subseteq E\implies \phi(A)\leq \phi(E)$,
    \item \textbf{stable} if $E\neq 0$ and $0\neq A\subsetneq E\implies \phi(A)< \phi(E)$,
    \item \textbf{polystable} if $E$ is a finite direct sum of stable objects of equal phase.
\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:33:21.485041+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0876afd796b8bfc599511bd3570d193cd72d6d77550ca9a72b7c7e3cb84d32e2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem Sharp small-hole eigenvalue asymptotic, \(d = 2\) of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let \(d = 2\) and \(\partial M\)
uniformly of class \(C^{1,1}\), and write
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = \operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)\).
The planar boundary layer has three regimes:

(i) boundary-scale centers,
\(\delta_{\varepsilon}/\varepsilon = O(1)\) (including
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = 0\)):

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right);\]

(ii) intermediate centers,
\(\varepsilon \ll \delta_{\varepsilon} \ll 1\) with
\(\theta: = limlog\left( 1/\delta_{\varepsilon} \right)/\log(1/\varepsilon) \in (0,1)\)
(equivalently
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = \varepsilon^{\theta + o(1)}\)):

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = B(\theta) \cdot \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right),\quad\quad B(\theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \theta};\]

(iii) macroscopically interior centers, \(\delta_{\varepsilon}\)
bounded below:

\[\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = \frac{\pi}{|M|\,\log(1/\varepsilon)}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right).\]

Here \(\theta \in \lbrack 0,1\rbrack\) is the logarithmic
boundary-layer parameter, with \(\theta = 0\) for macroscopically
interior centers (iii) and \(\theta = 1\) for boundary-scale
centers (i); the three regimes are the single asymptotic
\(\lambda\left( B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \right) = B(\theta)\,\pi/\left( |M|\log(1/\varepsilon) \right)\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\)
with \(B(\theta) = 1/(1 + \theta)\). The profile \(B\)
acts on the eigenvalue --- and, by Proposition D.5, on the Neumann
capacity --- decreasing from the interior value \(B(0) = 1\) to
the boundary value \(B(1) = \frac{1}{2}\); the associated
hitting-time constant of Corollary D.9 is the reciprocal
\(1/B(\theta) = 1 + \theta\), increasing from \(1\) to
\(2\). Thus a boundary-scale target has half the eigenvalue, and
twice the hitting time, of a macroscopically interior one. In contrast
to \(d \geq 3\), every fixed rescaled distance
\(\delta_{\varepsilon}/\varepsilon\) corresponds to
\(\theta = 1\) and hence to the same boundary value; the
nontrivial planar transition occurs only on the logarithmic scale
\(\theta\).","status":"unverified"}

\begin{enumerate}

$$

\item If $\gamma$ is of type $\operatorname{I}$ or $\operatorname{II}$ and if $t\in[0,1]\mapsto\mathscr{A}_\gamma(t)$ is decreasing, then 
 $$

Then: X_n => X in distribution implies g(X_n) => g(X); X_n -> X in probability implies g(X_n) -> g(X) in probability; X_n -> X almost surely implies g(X_n) -> g(X) almost surely. The hypothesis is that the LIMIT avoids the discontinuity set almost surely, not that g is continuous everywhere - which is what makes the theorem usable for maps such as x -> 1/x when the limit is almost surely nonzero, or x -> 1_{(a, infinity)}(x) when P(X = a) = 0. Without that hypothesis the conclusion fails: with X_n = 1/n deterministically, X = 0, and g = 1_{(0, infinity)}, we have g(X_n) = 1 for all n while g(X) = 0. D_g is always Borel for any g between metric spaces, so that part of the hypothesis is automatic. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.453874+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08cb2cce823e3ef90c0d4d8176c14e9e2ecaded0819ca030e68b0f0abce94635","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma eq:coord_redn_r_ineq1 of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:calYr_min_M2s}
Let $f \in \Sym^r$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item[(i)] If $r=0$, then $M_2(f) \ge 2$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_1^0$. 
\item[(ii)] If $r\in(0,1)$, then $M_2(f) \ge 2-2r+r^2 > 1$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_0^r$. 
\item[(iii)] If $r=1$, then $M_2(f) \ge 1$, with equality if and only if $f = \hat{f}_0^1$. 
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
First consider $r=0$. We compute
\begin{align}
M_2(f) 

= \sum_{\substack{z \in 2\mathbb{Z} \\ z \ne 0}} z^2 f(z)
&\ge \sum_{\substack{z \in 2\mathbb{Z} \\ z \ne 0}} 2^2 f(z)  \\
&= 4(1-f(0)) \nonumber \\

&= 4\bigg(1-\frac{1-\sum_{k \ge 2}\alpha_k^0}{2}\bigg) \\
&\ge 4\bigg(1-\frac{1}{2}\bigg) 
= 2 
= M_2(\hat{f}_1^0) .  
\end{align}
where we have used 
(thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper) in 
(equation eq:coord_redn_r_eq2 of the paper),
and (lem:calY_negative_coefficient_control of the paper) in (equation eq:coord_redn_r_ineq2 of the paper).
Equality is attained in (equation eq:coord_redn_r_ineq1 of the paper) only if $\supp(f) \subseteq \{0, \pm 2\}$; 
which forces $f = \hat{f}_1^0$ by 
(thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper).

Now consider $r \in (0,1)$. 

Noting that the four smallest elements in magnitude of $S^r = 2\mathbb{Z} + \{\pm r\}$ are $\{\pm r, \pm(2-r)\}$, we compute
\begin{align*}
M_2(f) 
&= \sum_{z \in S^r} z^2 f(z) \\

&\ge 

r^2(f(r)+f(-r)) + \sum_{\substack{z \in S^r \\ z \ne \pm r}} (2-r)^2 f(z) \\
&= r^2(f(r)+f(-r)) + (2-r)^2(1-f(r)-f(-r)) \\

&= 4(1-r)(1 - f(r) - f(-r)) + r^2 .
\end{align*}
By (lem:calY_negative_coefficient_control of the paper), 

\( 
\alpha_0^r +\alpha_1^r 
= 1-\sum_{\substack{k \in \mathbb{Z} \\ k \ne 0,1}} \alpha_k^r
\le 1,
\)
and 
$$f(r) 
= \alpha_0^r \hat{f}_0^r(r) + \alpha_1^r \hat{f}_1^r(r) 
= \alpha_0^r (\frac{q}{2}) + \alpha_1^r (\frac{p}{2})$$
and similarly 
$$f(-r) 
= \alpha_0^r \hat{f}_0^r(-r) + \alpha_1^r \hat{f}_1^r(-r) 
= \alpha_0^r (\frac{p}{2}) + \alpha_1^r (\frac{q}{2})$$
so that 
$f(r) + f(-r) 

= \frac{1}{2}(\alpha_0^r + \alpha_1^r)
\le \frac{1}{2}
$. 
Therefore
\begin{align*}
M_2(f) 
&\ge 4(1-r)(1-\frac{1}{2}) + r^2 
= 2(1-r) + r^2 

= M_2(\hat{f}_0^r) . 
\end{align*}
Equality is attained only if $\supp(f) \subseteq \{\pm r, \pm(2-r)\}$, which forces $f = \hat{f}_0^r$ by (thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper). 

Finally consider $r=1$. 
In this case $\supp(f) = 2\mathbb{Z}+\{1\}$, so 
\[ 
M_2(f) = \sum_{z \in \supp(f)} z^2 f(z) 
\ge \sum_{z \in \supp(f)} f(z) = 1 = M_2(\hat{f}_0^1). 
\]
In order to attain equality we need $z^2 = 1$ for every $z \in \supp(f)$; in this case $\supp(f) \subseteq \{\pm 1\}$ and $f = \hat{f}_0^1$ by (lem:support_size_one_or_two of the paper). 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:49:15.416016+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_08e731367b202eb8720e9876e297021caa7de2fe4ced011afeb645d84a309278","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.27904, 'Instantons, indefinite 4-manifolds, and Dehn surgery'] A \textit{stratified-smooth space} $(P,\Delta)$ (or simply $P$) of dimension $n$ is the following data: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item a partially ordered set $\Delta$ equipped with a dimension function $d: \Delta \to \mathbb N$ with maximum value $n$, 
		\item a compact topological space $P$ equipped with a partition into locally-closed subsets $P_\sigma$ for $\sigma \in \Delta$, satisfying $\overline P_\sigma = \bigcup_{\tau \le \sigma} P_\tau$, 
		\item the structure on each stratum $P_\sigma$ of a smooth manifold of dimension $d(\sigma)$.
	\end{itemize}
	We demand that the following {\it locally standard} hypothesis holds: for each $p \in P_\sigma$, there are non-negative integers $k$, $l$, an isomorphism of posets 
	$\bar \phi: \Delta_{\ge \sigma} \cong \{0,1\}^k$, an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$ in $P$, an open neighborhood $V$ of the origin in $[0,\infty)^k \times \mathbb R^{n+l-k}$, 
	a smooth map $\psi: V\to \mathbb R^l$, and a homeomorphism $\phi:U\to \psi^{-1}(0)$ with the following properties. For any stratum $Q_\sigma$ of $[0,\infty)^k \times \mathbb R^{n+l-k}$,
	the restriction of the map $\psi$ to $V\cap Q_\sigma$ is smooth and transverse to $0$. Furthermore, $\phi$ restricted to $P_\sigma$ takes values in 
	$V\cap Q_{\overline \phi(\sigma)}$ and this restriction is a diffeomorphism.
	
	A \textit{stratified-smooth $SO(3)$-space} is a stratified-smooth space $P$ equipped with a continuous $SO(3)$-action, for which each $P_\sigma$ is $SO(3)$-invariant, and the action is smooth on each stratum.

	A \textit{diffeomorphism} of stratified-smooth spaces $(\phi,\bar \phi): (P,\Delta)\to (P',\Delta')$  is the pair of an isomorphism of partially-ordered sets 
	$\bar \phi:\Delta \to \Delta'$ and a homeomorphism $\phi:P\to P'$ that restricts to a diffeomorphism from $P_\sigma$ to $P'_{\bar \phi(\sigma)}$ for each 
	$\sigma\in \Delta$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Omega is a bounded open subset of R^N with N >= 2 and 1 < p < N","a(x,s,xi) is a Caratheodory Leray-Lions field: p-growth with k in L^{p'}, coercivity a.xi >= alpha |xi|^p, strict monotonicity in xi","f in L^1(Omega); the estimates are on weak solutions of approximating problems with L^1-bounded data","existence of a distributional W_0^{1,q} solution additionally needs p > 2 - 1/N","homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:23.251071+00:00","domain":"nonlinear elliptic PDE, L^1 data, truncation method, Marcinkiewicz estimates","id":"claim_091da16d48d2aaf84660ce50e0a871758dac4023b0cb663a0df7ad63ba360344","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Setting: $\\Omega \\subset \\mathbb{R}^N$ bounded open, $N \\geq 2$, $1 < p < N$. Let $a: \\Omega\\times\\mathbb{R}\\times\\mathbb{R}^N \\to \\mathbb{R}^N$ be a Caratheodory function (measurable in $x$, continuous in $(s,\\xi)$) satisfying, for a.e. $x$ and all $s, \\xi, \\eta$: growth $|a(x,s,\\xi)| \\leq \\beta\\,(k(x) + |s|^{p-1} + |\\xi|^{p-1})$ with $k \\in L^{p'}(\\Omega)$; coercivity $a(x,s,\\xi)\\cdot\\xi \\geq \\alpha|\\xi|^p$ with $\\alpha > 0$; strict monotonicity $(a(x,s,\\xi) - a(x,s,\\eta))\\cdot(\\xi-\\eta) > 0$ for $\\xi \\neq \\eta$ (a Leray-Lions operator, e.g. the $p$-Laplacian $a = |\\xi|^{p-2}\\xi$). Consider $-\\operatorname{div}\\,a(x,u,\\nabla u) = f$ in $\\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\\partial\\Omega$, with $f \\in L^1(\\Omega)$. (Boccardo-Gallouet, J. Funct. Anal. 87 (1989); the estimates are the nonlinear form of Stampacchia's truncation estimates.) A PRIORI ESTIMATES. Let $u \\in W_0^{1,p}(\\Omega)$ be a weak solution for a datum $f \\in L^1 \\cap W^{-1,p'}$ (in practice the solutions $u_n$ of approximating problems with $f_n \\in L^\\infty$, $\\|f_n\\|_{L^1} \\leq \\|f\\|_{L^1}$; all constants below depend only on $N, p, \\alpha, \\|f\\|_{L^1}$, never on $n$). Then: (E1) for every $k > 0$, $\\alpha\\int_\\Omega|\\nabla T_k(u)|^p\\,dx \\leq k\\,\\|f\\|_{L^1}$; (E2) for every $k > 0$, $|\\{|u| \\geq k\\}| \\leq (S^p\\|f\\|_{L^1}/\\alpha)^{N/(N-p)}\\,k^{-N(p-1)/(N-p)}$, where $S$ is the Sobolev constant of $W_0^{1,p} \\hookrightarrow L^{p^*}$, $p^* = Np/(N-p)$; i.e. $u$ is bounded in the Marcinkiewicz space $M^{N(p-1)/(N-p)}(\\Omega)$; (E3) for every $h > 0$, $|\\{|\\nabla u| \\geq h\\}| \\leq C\\,h^{-N(p-1)/(N-1)}$, i.e. $|\\nabla u|$ is bounded in $M^{N(p-1)/(N-1)}(\\Omega)$; hence, $\\Omega$ being bounded, $u$ is bounded in $W_0^{1,q}(\\Omega)$ for every $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$. EXISTENCE. If moreover $p > 2 - 1/N$ (equivalently $N(p-1)/(N-1) > 1$), there exists $u \\in W_0^{1,q}(\\Omega)$ for every $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$, with $T_k(u) \\in W_0^{1,p}(\\Omega)$ for every $k$, $a(x,u,\\nabla u) \\in L^{r}(\\Omega)$ for some $r > 1$, and $\\int_\\Omega a(x,u,\\nabla u)\\cdot\\nabla\\varphi\\,dx = \\int_\\Omega f\\varphi\\,dx$ for all $\\varphi \\in C_c^\\infty(\\Omega)$ (a distributional solution). For $p = 2$ this is exactly Stampacchia's $q < N/(N-1)$. Sharp edges: (a) $q = N(p-1)/(N-1)$ is not attained - the fundamental solution of the $p$-Laplacian with $f = \\delta_0$ has $|\\nabla u| \\sim |x|^{-(N-1)/(p-1)}$, in $L^q$ iff $q < N(p-1)/(N-1)$; (b) for $1 < p \\leq 2 - 1/N$ the gradient of the solution is in general NOT in $L^1$, $u \\notin W^{1,1}$, and the distributional formulation is meaningless - one must use entropy or renormalized solutions defined through the truncations $T_k(u) \\in W_0^{1,p}$ and a generalized gradient; (c) existence is asserted, uniqueness is NOT: distributional $W^{1,q}$ solutions need not be unique (Serrin's pathological solutions of $\\operatorname{div}(A\\nabla u) = 0$ with $u \\in W^{1,q}$, $q < 2$, $u \\notin H^1_{loc}$, already for $p = 2$ and measurable coefficients); uniqueness holds in the entropy-solution class (Benilan, Boccardo, Gallouet, Gariepy, Pierre, Vazquez 1995) for $L^1$ data; (d) the estimates (E1)-(E3) require $T_k(u)$ to be an admissible test function, which is why they are proved on the approximations; (e) for measure data one gets the same $W_0^{1,q}$ bounds, but for a measure concentrated on a set of zero $p$-capacity the entropy uniqueness theory does not apply.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:38:11.735717+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_092f647668962c58af82e5e5f77ed3d543aea8d38795a25920ac1a86802cdd53","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:complex_cumu of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] (Complex cumulant expansion) 
		Let $h$ be a complex random variable all of whose moments exist. The $(p,q)$-cumulant of $h$ is defined as
		$$
		\mathcal{C}^{(p,q)}(h)\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.65ex \lineskiplimit0pt \hbox{.}\hbox{.}}}= (-\mathrm{i})^{p+q} \cdot \left(\frac{\partial^{p+q}}{\partial {s^p} \partial {t^q}} \log \mathbb{E} e^{\mathrm{i}sh+\mathrm{i}t\overline{h}}\right) \bigg{|}_{s=t=0}\,.
		$$
		Let $f:\mathbb C^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth function, and we denote its holomorphic  derivatives by
		$$
		f^{(p,q)}(z_1,z_2)\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.65ex \lineskiplimit0pt \hbox{.}\hbox{.}}}= \frac{\partial^{p+q}}{\partial z_1^p \partial z_2^q} f(z_1,z_2)\,.
		$$ Then, for any fixed $l \in \mathbb{N}$, we have
		\begin{equation} 
		\mathbb{E} f(h,\overline{h})\overline{h}=\sum\limits_{p+q=0}^l \frac{1}{p!\,q!}\mathcal{C}^{(p,q+1)}(h)\mathbb{E} f^{(p,q)}(h,\overline{h}) + R_{l+1}\,,
		\end{equation}
		given all integrals in ((5.16 of the paper)) exist. Here, $R_{l+1}$ is the remainder term depending on $f$ and $h$, and for any $\tau>0$, we have the estimate
		$$
			\begin{aligned}
			R_{l+1}=&\, \mathrm{O}(1)\cdot \mathbb{E} \big|h^{l+2}\mathbf{1}_{\{|h|>N^{\tau-1/2}\}}\big|\cdot \max\limits_{p+q=l+1}\big\| f^{(p,q)}(z,\overline{z})\big\|_{\infty} \\
			+&\,\mathrm{O}(1) \cdot \mathbb{E} |h|^{l+2} \cdot \max\limits_{p+q=l+1}\big\| f^{(p,q)}(z,\overline{z})\cdot \mathbf{1}_{\{|z|\le N^{\tau-1/2}\}}\big\|_{\infty}\,.
			\end{aligned}
		$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:09:59.188980+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0935d8c0dfb8300de8ce81d192e6cb1afc0aca7c9668dc92e877c9391089a3a4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:Qh-monotonicity of arXiv:2608.05262, 'The law of $(1+1)$D SOS with an area tilt in a wedge'] {HKS25}}]
    
    Consider laws $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$
    on 
    
    ordered random walk curves $X_1 \ge \cdots \ge X_K$ on interval $I\subset \mathbb Z$, 
    parametrized by curves $g(x) \ge h(x)$ on $I$,  
    boundary values $\underline{u}, \underline{v} \in \mathbb Z^K$ and 
    area-tilt $\underline{b}=\{b_i(x),  x \in I,  1 \le i \le K\}$,  such that:
    \begin{itemize}
    \item The ordered curves $X_1(x)\geq \cdots \geq X_K(x)$ for all $x\in I$ have a global ceiling 
    $g(\cdot) \le \infty$ and floor $h(\cdot) \ge - \infty$ (i.e.,  $X_1 \leq g$ and $X_K \geq h$).
    \item The curves have boundary conditions $\underline{u},\underline{v}$, each of which is either ordered (e.g., $\underline{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)$ where $u_i\geq u_{i+1}$) or free.
    \item The law of the increment $\mathfrak{X}\in \mathbb Z$ for curve $1\leq i\leq K$ at location $x\in I$ may depend on $i,x$ as long as it is of the form $\mathbb P(\mathfrak X_{i,x}=k) = \exp(-f_{i,x}(k))$ for a convex function $f_{i,x}$ which is finite at
 least when $k \in \pm 1$.
    \item The area tilt of curve $1\leq i\leq K$ at location $x\in I$ may depend on $i,x$,  of the form $\exp(-b_{i}(x) X_i(x))$.
    \end{itemize} 
    If the parameters of $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$ are such that
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item the ceilings and floors are ordered: $g^\uparrow\geq g^\downarrow$ and $h^\uparrow\geq h^\downarrow$ coordinate-wise; \item the boundary conditions are ordered: $\underline{u}^\uparrow\geq \underline{u}^\downarrow$ coordinate-wise or both are free, the same applies to $\underline{v}$;
    \item the area tilts are reversely-ordered:  $b_i^\uparrow(x) \leq b_i^\downarrow(x)$ for all $i,x$;
    \end{enumerate} 
    then there is a coupling of $\mathbb Q^\uparrow,\mathbb Q^\downarrow$  so that $X_i^\uparrow(x)\geq X_i^\downarrow(x)$ for all $1\leq i\leq K$ and $x\in I$.","status":"unverified"}

\begin{proof} Consider any $\YY$ belonging to the set on the left-hand side of the above display. By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
    \[
        \Budget(\YY;\mu) \le \frac{1}{\alpha} (\mu,\vwww) = \frac{1}{\alpha}\,,

    This further implies (recalling $\iota,\epsilon \le 1$)

{"assumptions":["X is a compact metric space and T is continuous","the metric is fixed, but the notions defined are independent of the choice of a compatible metric on a compact space","Gamma_eps(x) is taken with forward iterates for a general continuous map and with two-sided iterates for a homeomorphism","Bowen's entropy h(T,Y) is used for arbitrary, possibly non-invariant, subsets Y"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090635+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_09ce2d5bcd2dcfca590ed7dbdf3202b050716fcf7e9c95e3a6d615cdc80401f0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. For a subset Y of X (not assumed invariant or closed) Bowen's entropy of T on Y is h(T, Y) = lim as delta -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r_n(delta, Y), where r_n(delta, Y) is the least cardinality of a set S that (n, delta)-spans Y, that is such that every y in Y admits s in S with d(T^i y, T^i s) <= delta for all 0 <= i < n. For eps > 0 and x in X put Gamma_eps(x) = { y in X : d(T^i x, T^i y) <= eps for all i >= 0 }, the set of points whose forward orbit shadows that of x at scale eps (for a homeomorphism one lets i range over all integers). DEFINITIONS: T is h-EXPANSIVE (Bowen) if there exists eps > 0 with h(T, Gamma_eps(x)) = 0 for every x in X. The TAIL ENTROPY of T is h*(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of sup over x in X of h(T, Gamma_eps(x)); the limit exists because the supremum is nondecreasing in eps. T is ASYMPTOTICALLY h-EXPANSIVE (Misiurewicz) if h*(T) = 0. Relations and cautions: expansive implies h-expansive (for small eps the sets Gamma_eps(x) are singletons, with the one- or two-sided convention matching the map), and h-expansive implies asymptotically h-expansive; neither implication reverses. Subshifts and expanding maps are expansive, hence h-expansive; every C^infinity diffeomorphism of a compact manifold is asymptotically h-expansive (Newhouse), while for finite smoothness this can fail. The quantity h*(T) measures the entropy invisible at any finite scale - the entropy 'in the tail' - and it is zero exactly when the system admits a principal symbolic extension (Boyle-Downarowicz theory); it is not the same as the topological entropy and carries no information about it.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.476862+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_09ef64e39f8041b11f5d7d5d89986a034f527c9a0cf757fad1cde849f5115bd2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem eq:symm_4q_special of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] In $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$ with $2 \nmid q$, there exist symmetrization resistant random variables for which the minimum-entropy independent symmetrizer is not unique. 

\begin{proof}
In $\mathbb{Z}_3$, writing PMFs as $z = (z(-1),z(0),z(1))$, we see that $f = \frac{1}{3}(1,2,0)$ (which is symmetrization resistant by (thm:Z3 of the paper)) has $\frac{1}{3}(2,0,1)$ and $\frac{1}{3}(0,2,1)$ as symmetrizers. 

In $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$,
$f = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{q})$ 
has equal-entropy symmetrizers 
$f_{-} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{3q})$
and
$g = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{2q})$. 

Note that $h \in \Sym(f)$ if and only if for all $s \in [4q]$
\begin{equation}
h(s) + h(s-q) = h(-s) + h(-s-q) 
\end{equation}
so that if $h(s) > \frac{1}{2}$ for some $s$, we have 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(s) \le h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
and therefore 
\[ 1 < h(s) + h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
so that either $s = -s$ (so $s = 0$) or $s = -s-q$ (so $2s = q$). 
Since $2$ does not divide $q$, the latter cannot happen and we need only consider $s=0$.
Evaluating (equation eq:symm_4q_special of the paper) at $s=q$ yields
\[ h(q) + h(0) = h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
so that 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(0) \le h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
and since $0$, $-q$, and $-2q$ are distinct modulo $4q$, we obtain 
\[ 1 < h(0) + h(-q) + h(-2q) \le \sum_x h(x) = 1 , \]
a contradiction. 
Thus $h \le \frac{1}{2}$ everywhere and
\[ H(h) = \sum_{x}h(x) \log_2\bigg(\frac{1}{h(x)}\bigg) \ge \sum_{x} h(x) = 1 = H(f), \]
so our $f$ is symmetrization resistant. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

A set of Latin squares, all of the same order, all pairs of which are orthogonal is called a set of mutually orthogonal Latin squares. This concept of orthogonality in combinatorics is strongly related to the concept of blocking in statistics, which ensures that independent variables are truly independent with no hidden confounding correlations. \"Orthogonal\" is thus synonymous with \"independent\" in that knowing one variable's value gives no further information about another variable's likely value.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.497230+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0a13feb8b6c2da5875bf465be8e3a647d826169e7400caa42c4687fc7952300e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm commutation_relation_u of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $n$ radial SLEs start at $e^{i\theta_1}, e^{i\theta_2}, \ldots, e^{i\theta_n} \in \partial \mathbb{D}$, with a marked interior point \( u \neq 0 \).

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] For \( u = e^{i v} \), let the infinitesimal diffusion generators be
    \[
    \mathcal{M}_i = \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} + b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \partial_i + \sum_{j \neq i} \cot\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_j + \cot\left(\frac{v - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_v + \cot\left(\frac{\overline{v} - \theta_i}{2}\right) \overline{\partial}_v.
    \]
    If the $n$ SLEs locally commute, the generators satisfy:
    \[
    [\mathcal{M}_i, \mathcal{M}_j] = \frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right)} (\mathcal{M}_j - \mathcal{M}_i).
    \]
    There exists a partition function \(\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u)\) such that the drift term \( b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \) is given by
    \[
    b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) = \kappa \partial_i \log \psi,
    \]
    and \(\psi\) satisfies the null vector equations:
    \[
    \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} \psi + \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{2}{\theta_j - \theta_i} \partial_i \psi + \frac{2}{v - \theta_i} \partial_v \psi + \frac{2}{\overline{v} - \theta_i} \overline{\partial}_v \psi + \left[\left(1 - \frac{6}{\kappa}\right) \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{1}{(\theta_j - \theta_i)^2} + h_i(\theta_i, u)\right] \psi = 0.
    \]

    \item[(ii)] By analyzing the asymptotics of adjacent points \( \theta_i \) and \( \theta_{i+1} \), we deduce that \( h_i(\theta, u) = h_{i+1}(\theta, u) \). If all points are consecutive, there exists a common function \( h(\theta, u) \) such that
    \[
    h(\theta, u) = h_1(\theta, u) = \cdots = h_n(\theta, u).
    \]

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f_n -> f in measure or mu-almost everywhere","uniform integrability of {f_n}","uniform tightness of {f_n}: on an infinite measure space this is an independent hypothesis"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751693+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_0a5d28e3a2f0563534ddca90e6e5c1998a87b5c53300e2cd9dcf829e15f851d8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"On a FINITE measure space, uniform integrability plus convergence in measure gives L^1 convergence. On a general (for instance sigma-finite but infinite) measure space this is FALSE and a third hypothesis is needed. The correct statement: let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and f_n in L^1(mu) with f_n -> f in measure (or mu-a.e.). Then f_n -> f in L^1(mu) if and only if (i) {f_n} is uniformly integrable, meaning sup_n integral_{|f_n| > K} |f_n| dmu -> 0 as K -> infinity, AND (ii) {f_n} is uniformly tight, meaning for every eps > 0 there is a set A with mu(A) < infinity and sup_n integral_{Omega \\ A} |f_n| dmu < eps. Counterexample showing (ii) is not implied by (i): on R with Lebesgue measure take f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}. Then |f_n| <= 1 so the family is uniformly integrable and dominated, f_n -> 0 pointwise everywhere, yet ||f_n||_1 = 1 for every n. Mass escapes to infinity; on a finite measure space it has nowhere to go, which is exactly why the finite-measure statement can omit (ii). [standard; e.g. Bogachev, Measure Theory, Vol. I, Section 4.5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.256291+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0a60fd160e84429e26bd981f1133f3bc1725ae3b7b6dab59d1a3e3e6350bed50","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem ASASiid of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] There exists a sequence of deterministic values, called {Lyapunov exponents}
	\[
	\lambda_k < \cdots < \lambda_1, \qquad \lambda_i \in [-\infty, \infty),
	\]
	and a set of full measure $\tilde{\Omega} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B}$ with respect to $\mu \times \mathbf{P}$ such that 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The set $\tilde{\Omega}$ is $\Theta_t$-invariant for every $t \ge 0$.  
		For each $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, define
		\[
		G_\lambda(\omega,x) := \left\{ z \in \mathbb{R}^d : 
		\limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| \le \lambda \right\}.
		\]
		Then $G_{\lambda_1}(\omega, x) = \mathbb{R}^d$, and for every $1 \le i < k$,
		\[
		z \in G_{\lambda_i}(\omega,x) \setminus G_{\lambda_{i+1}}(\omega,x)
		\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_i.
		\]
		Moreover, for all $z \in G_{\lambda_k}(\omega,x) \setminus \{0\}$,
		\[
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_k.
		\]
		\item Suppose $\lambda_1 < 0$ and that for some $r \in (0,1]$ and all $y,z \in \mathbb{R}^d$ there exist constants $\overline{C}_F > 0$ and $p_1 \ge 1$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			\| \mathrm{D}_y F - \mathrm{D}_z F \|_{L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)}
			\le \overline{C}_F (1 + |y| + |z|)^{p_1} |y-z|^r.
		\end{equation}
		Then there exists a full-measure set $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega$ such that, for every $0 < \nu < -\lambda_1$, there exists a positive random variable
		\begin{align}
			R^\nu : \mathcal{M} \to (0,\infty)
		\end{align}
		with the property that for all $(x,\omega) \in \mathcal{M}$ and all $y \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $|y| \le R^\nu(x,\omega)$,
		\[
		\sup_{t \ge 0} \exp(t\nu) \, \big| \Phi^t_\omega(x+y) - \Phi^t_\omega(x) \big| < \infty.
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["i.i.d. rows C^{1/2} z with z having i.i.d. mean-zero unit-variance entries and finite twelfth moment","p/n -> q_0 in (0, infinity)","the population spectral distribution converges to a limit with bounded support","the formula is used inside the bulk; isolated spikes are handled by the BBP correction"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T05:50:37.943602+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_0a70bf7dec2d4a8e97f8b3a3a903aaf467d73a6d689fe2fb896f6788c775985a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $E = \\frac{1}{n} X^T X$ be the sample covariance of $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $C$ (rows $C^{1/2} z_i$ with $z_i$ having i.i.d. entries of mean zero, variance one and finite twelfth moment), in the regime $p, n \\to \\infty$ with $q = p/n \\to q_0 \\in (0, \\infty)$, and assume the spectral distribution of $C$ converges to a limit with bounded support. Let $\\lambda_k, u_k$ be the sample eigenvalues and eigenvectors and let $g_E(z) = \\frac{1}{p}\\operatorname{tr}(z I - E)^{-1}$ be the Stieltjes transform of the sample spectrum, with $g(\\lambda - i0) := \\lim_{\\eta \\downarrow 0} g_E(\\lambda - i\\eta)$ inside the bulk. THEOREM (Ledoit and Peche, 2011, Theorem 4; in the form of Bun, Bouchaud and Potters 2017). The oracle eigenvalues $\\xi_k^{\\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$ converge, uniformly in $k$ inside the bulk, to $$\\xi(\\lambda_k) = \\frac{\\lambda_k}{\\big|\\, 1 - q + q\\, \\lambda_k\\, g_E(\\lambda_k - i0) \\,\\big|^2}.$$ This limit depends on the population covariance $C$ only through the observable sample spectrum, so it is a consistent, computable estimator (the rotationally invariant estimator, RIE, or nonlinear shrinkage): replace each sample eigenvalue by $\\xi(\\lambda_k)$, keep the sample eigenvectors. In practice $g_E$ is evaluated at $\\lambda_k - i\\eta$ with a small $\\eta$ of order $n^{-1/2}$ times the eigenvalue scale, and the result is floored at a small positive fraction of the bulk level. When $C = \\sigma^2 I$ the formula returns $\\sigma^2$ for every eigenvalue (the Marchenko-Pastur spread is entirely removed); for a spike above the bulk it returns approximately the debiased population spike. Applying the formula to a matrix whose largest eigenvalue is a signal one is trying to keep, and flooring relative to that top eigenvalue, destroys the small eigenvalues that the inverse depends on.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["K compact and convex in a locally convex Hausdorff space","K metrizable for the measure to live on ext K itself"],"created_at":"2026-08-29T02:26:24.139081+00:00","domain":"functional analysis / convexity","id":"claim_0a8ceaa5f37b374709515e490798b2dbcdf330a9987e8089bd7542bf2dd180cd","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let K be a compact convex subset of a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space, and suppose K is metrizable. Then the set ext K of extreme points of K is a G_delta set, and for every x in K there is a Borel probability measure mu on K, concentrated on ext K, whose barycenter is x: phi(x) = integral phi dmu for every continuous linear functional phi. Without metrizability, the Bishop-de Leeuw theorem gives a probability measure that vanishes on every Baire set disjoint from ext K. The Krein-Milman theorem, that K is the closed convex hull of ext K, is the qualitative counterpart. Uniqueness of the representing measure for every x characterises the Choquet simplices.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Zero-mean fixed finite-rank GP, supplied feature norms <=R, independent Gaussian noise variance s>0","At most n context labels; all input locations and context length jointly independent of latent GP and noises; iid tasks","Full original posterior is the target; only the predictor clips context labels at the explicit deterministic B"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:46:14.074691+00:00","domain":"Gaussian process predictive approximation; context truncation","id":"claim_0aac28c997e413b6e870c7d366e02430c9ded09828abe71420cb34a1f75fae4a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"OWNER RESULT DRAFT, proof (unaudited), C007 v1; no novelty claim.
Let a fixed zero-mean finite-rank Gaussian process have a supplied feature map phi with ||phi(x)||<=R, independent Gaussian observation noise of variance s>0, and at most n context observations. All context/query input locations and context length are jointly independent of the GP and all noises. Context labels may be correlated and are not bounded or conditioned. Put V=s+R^2. Given the full original context W, let P_W=N(m,v) be the exact noisy posterior predictive. Clip each context label to [-B,B], B>0, and recompute the mean m_B with the same design; v is unchanged. Suppose a Gaussian predictor h_B=N(mhat,vhat), depending only on clipped context and supplied features, has vhat>=s and KL(N(m_B,v)||h_B)<=eps_c for every possible context and design. Then on the ORIGINAL unconditioned task law,
E_W KL(P_W||h_B) <= 2 eps_c + (2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^3) exp(-B^2/(4V)).
In particular, for eps>0, eps_c=eps/4 and B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,4 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/(s^3 eps)))) make the expected KL at most eps. If nR=0 the bias is zero. This does not assert that N(m_B,v) is the conditional law given clipped labels. The supplied-feature comparator exists by the separately audited C002 construction; this clipping lemma itself awaits independent review.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.911750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0aaecc49d44d87907f247a5d4649f0d44cb4b47482a6a7ec68426e9191e0ff9a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 1 (Criterion for $\Xstar_T$ {\cite[Lemma~4.1) of arXiv:2608.24294, 'Existence of densities and atoms for the running maximum of time-inhomogeneous jump diffus'] {NakagawaSuzuki2024}}]
Fix $p>1$ and $\Theta=(h,v)\in \Hb_{\infty-}\times \Vb_{\infty-}$.
For each $n\ge1$, let $\{X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process, and let $\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process.
Write
\[
\Xstarn_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X^{(n)}_s,
\qquad
\Xstar_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X_s.
\]

Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E[|\Xstarn_T|^p]<\infty$, and for every $t\in[0,T]$ we have $X^{(n)}_t\in W^{1,p}_\Theta$ with
\[
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|D_\Theta X^{(n)}_s|^p\Big]<\infty;
\]
\item for each $n\ge1$, the process $\{D_\Theta X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ admits a right-continuous version;
\item $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|X^{(n)}_s-X_s|^p\Big]=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume moreover that $D_\Theta X$ admits a right-continuous version and satisfies
\[
\Pbb\big(D_\Theta X_t\neq 0 \text{ on }\{t\in(0,T]: X_t=\Xstar_T\}\big)=1.

{"assumptions":["Finite-dimensional Euclidean space; n>=2 components and K>=2 epochs","Convex C1 f_i with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradients, L_i>0","Proper closed convex psi and an attained finite minimum of F=f+psi","x_1 is in dom psi; eta is constant, positive, and satisfies the displayed K-dependent cap","For the expected random-reshuffling bound, use fresh independent uniform permutations","For the optimized-rate corollaries assume D>0; the fixed-step inequalities do not require D>0"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T15:34:11.132651+00:00","domain":"Liu Zhou; proximal shuffling; random reshuffling; last iterate; convex optimization","id":"claim_0ab04f1d8562a58b42caeb8c92cdff50dfe5a30627a7b67abd496813c58be7c6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let n>=2, K>=2 and d>=1. Let each f_i:R^d->R be convex C1 with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradient, L_i>0. Let psi:R^d->R union {+infinity} be proper closed convex. Set f=(1/n)sum_i f_i, F=f+psi, and suppose x* minimizes F with F(x*) finite. Start at x_1 in dom psi. Write D=||x_1-x*||, Lbar=(1/n)sum_i L_i, Lmax=max_i L_i, s=1+log K, sigma_any^2=(1/n)sum_i ||grad f_i(x*)||^2 and sigma_rand^2=sigma_any^2+n||grad f(x*)||^2. Use a fixed positive step eta<=1/[4n sqrt(2 Lbar Lmax s)]. In epoch k, set z_0=x_k, take z_i=z_(i-1)-eta grad f_(sigma_i)(z_(i-1)) for i=1,...,n along a permutation sigma, and set x_(k+1)=prox_(n eta psi)(z_n), where prox_(n eta psi)(z) minimizes psi(x)+||x-z||^2/(2n eta). There is an absolute constant C such that, for every sequence of permutations, F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+(n eta)^2 Lbar sigma_any^2 s]. If fresh independent uniform permutations are used in each epoch, E[F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)]<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+n eta^2 Lbar sigma_rand^2 s]. These are bounds for the last epoch iterate, with no strong-convexity assumption. For D>0, balancing eta under the stated cap gives respectively O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_any^2 s)^(1/3)/K^(2/3)) and O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_rand^2 s)^(1/3)/(n^(1/3) K^(2/3))). The fixed-step bounds also cover D=0. All norms are Euclidean. Source: Zijian Liu and Zhengyuan Zhou, On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Shuffling Gradient Methods, Theorem 4.4 and its full version Theorem C.1.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T11:58:53.978374+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ab65f335e4846d89753e7dca87d1223","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Exact rank three for the bounded-density conjecture: what is proved and what is open. (1) The step 'a rank-three coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K ||rho||_inf^{2/3} for S = sum_{j<=3} lambda_j Y_j^2' is false for general bounded densities rho on R^3: a density rho <= B that puts mass 2hB A(s) on the shell {|S - s| < h} gives p_S about B A(s) near s, where A(s) = d/ds vol{S <= s} = 2 pi s^{1/2}/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_3) for a definite form, unbounded as s grows; a bound needs regularity of rho beyond its supremum. (2) Orthonormal 3D projections of product densities have that regularity on spheres: their spherical means satisfy M_{y0}(r) <= 6/(pi r) uniformly in the centre, and definite rank-three forms have density <= 82 for every linear term. (3) The marginal bound is sharp and law-free: the projection onto a k-dimensional subspace of a vector with independent coordinates of densities <= 1 has density <= min{(n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2}} (Livshyts, Paouris and Pivovarov 2016); Ball's cube slicing is the uniform case and Rudelson-Vershynin give (CK)^d with an unspecified absolute C. (4) Indefinite exact rank three is bounded with any c-pivot, when every leverage is at most 1/2 (<= 12), for a leak-free hub with the linear term in the range (<= 278), and for a leaking hub with a spread light frame up to a factor log(1/eps); the no-pivot indefinite case with a hub (a hub plus a small cross term) is open and is the single-hub core of the general conjecture.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.211852+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ac6c86f902d62b5037f21bb5d2b9e94b3dc420f9686cffab5c2fcd0a8d5005a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix constants $C',c', K>0$. 
Let $X$ be a nonnegative random variable such that $\E X \leq r$ and, for some $\sigma \in (0,K]$, 
\[
\P(X>u ) \leq C' e^{- c' u^2/\sigma^2}\,.
\]
Then for each $\lambda>0$, there exist constants $C_\lambda, c_\lambda>0$ (depending also on $c',C'$, and $K$) such that
\[
  \E e^{\lambda X}-1 \leq C_\lambda r + C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
\]
\begin{proof}
On the event $\{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}\}$, the mean value theorem yields
\[
  \E[(e^{\lambda X} - 1) \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq \E[\lambda e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}} X \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda r\,,
\]
where the $\sigma$ independence in the last bound comes from $\sigma\leq K$.
On  $\{X > \sigma^{1/2}\}$, we write
\begin{multline}
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] - (e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}}-1)\P(X>\sigma^{1/2})
  \\
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \int_0^x \partial_u (e^{\lambda u}) \d u ~\d \P_X(x)  
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \P(X>u) \lambda e^{\lambda u} \d  u  \leq C_\lambda \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} e^{-c'\frac{u^2}{\sigma^2} + \lambda u} \d u\,.
\end{multline}
Now, for $u\geq \sigma^{1/2}$ and $\lambda>0$, there exists $\sigma_\lambda>0$ such that for all $\sigma \in (0,\sigma_\lambda]$, we have 
$
  \lambda u \leq \tfrac{c' u^2}{2\sigma^2}$.
For such $\sigma$, it follows from \eqref{eq:layer-cake} that
$
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
$
For $\sigma >\sigma_\lambda$, note that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:layer-cake} can be bounded by a constant $C_\lambda'>0$ times the Laplace transform of a Gaussian with variance $K^2/2c'$
to get 
$\E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda$,
possibly enlarging $C_\lambda$ from before.
We finish by multiplying by $e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma} e^{c_\lambda/\sigma_\lambda}$, which is larger than $1$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is continuous on a closed cylinder around (t_0,y_0)","f is Lipschitz in y, uniformly in t, on that cylinder"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T14:20:41.451641+00:00","domain":"ordinary differential equations","id":"claim_0ad98344cc4c4b7f94070b09639fced6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f: [t_0-a,t_0+a] x B(y_0,b) -> R^n be continuous, where B(y_0,b) subset R^n is the closed ball of radius b around y_0, and suppose f is Lipschitz in its second argument uniformly in the first: there is L >= 0 with |f(t,y_1)-f(t,y_2)| <= L|y_1-y_2| for all t in the interval and y_1,y_2 in B(y_0,b). Let M = max|f(t,y)| over this compact domain and h = min(a, b/M). Then the initial value problem y'(t) = f(t,y(t)), y(t_0)=y_0, has a unique solution y on [t_0-h, t_0+h]. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.525682+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ae1b4267139277f9deeb412aaabc6ee6c548ef0d00de6bde7b964ee7ab405b2","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition eq:third_renormalisation of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] For $i \geq 0$ and for $c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}$ as in \thref{prop:tile_and_cell_volume_bounds}, we let 
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \rho_i 
        = 
       
            1 - (i+s)^{-3/2}/2
      
        ,
        \quad
        \xi_i
        = 
        (i +1+ s)^{-3/2}/4,
        \quad
        \text{and}
        \quad
        C_i
        =
        c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}
        (m_i/2)^d.
    \end{equation}
    
    We say that a level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if it contains a cluster $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}$ satisfying
    
    \begin{equation}
        \# 
        \left(
            \mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap
            B(x_{0,j},r_0/4)
        \right)
        \geq 
        \nu 
        \# B(r_0/2),
    \end{equation}
    
    where $\nu$ is as in \thref{prop:biskup}.
    
    For a good level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$, the \textbf{good part} is $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap
            B(x_{0,j},r_0/4)$.
    
    We say that a level-$1$ tile $\Tile{1}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_1$ proportion of its level-$0$ subtiles are good, and their good parts are connected to each other inside $\Tile{1}{j}$.
    
    For a good level-$1$ tile $\Tile{1}{j}$, we choose $C_1$ of its good level-$0$ subtiles and the \textbf{good part} of $\Tile{1}{j}$ is the union of the good parts of these subtiles, denoted by $\mathcal{C}_{1,j}$.
    
    For $i \geq 2$, we say that level-$i$ tile $\Tile{i}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_i$ proportion of its level-$i-1$ subtiles are good, and additionally: 
    
    if $\Tile{i-2}{j}$ is a good level-$i-2$ subtile in a good level-$i-1$ subtile of $\Tile{i}{j}$, 
    
    and $\Tile{i-2}{k}$ is a good level-$i-2$ subtile in some other good level-$i-1$ subtile of $\Tile{i}{j}$, 
    
    then the good parts of $\Tile{i-2}{j}$ and $\Tile{i-2}{k}$ are connected in $\Tile{i}{j}$.
    
    For a good level-$i$ tile $\Tile{i}{j}$, we choose $C_i$ of its good level-$i-1$ subtiles and the \textbf{good part} of $\Tile{i}{j}$ is the union of the good parts of these subtiles, denoted by $\mathcal{C}_{i,j}$.
    
    When choosing the good part of $\Tile{i}{j}$, if the subtile containing the origin $o$ is good, we choose it to be part of the good part.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.124772+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_0af7f08c031d42588951778c44187958","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In commutative algebra and algebraic geometry, localization is a formal way to introduce the \"denominators\" to a given ring or module. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.501965+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afdafd4b352c5fcad844d588f8048f7a3634622f9b8b5964f08fe8ff6f0d068","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theo 22 (Explicit threshold, compact-support branch and onset amplitude) of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $0<\alpha<1$ and $n\ge2$. Consider the problem
\[
\begin{cases}
	-u''=\lambda u+m_n(x)u^\alpha,& -1<x<1,\\
	u(-1)=u(1)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
\lambda_{c,n}:=
\frac{\pi^2}
{\left((1-\alpha)+\dfrac{1+\alpha}{n}\right)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\pi^2}{4}
<
\lambda_{c,n}
<
\lambda_n^*.
\]
At $\lambda=\lambda_{c,n}$ there exists an even positive flat solution
$u_{c,n}$ satisfying $u_{c,n}(\pm1)=u_{c,n}'(\pm1)=0$. For every
$\lambda\in(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$ there exists a unique even
non-negative solution in the above class whose connected support is
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_{\lambda,n}
=
[-b_{\lambda,n},b_{\lambda,n}]
\Subset(-1,1),
\]
where
\[
b_{\lambda,n}
=
\frac{1}{1-\alpha}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\lambda}}
-\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right).
\]
For $x\ge0$ the solution is
\[
u_{\lambda,n}(x)
=
\begin{cases}
	A_{\lambda,n}\cos(\sqrt{\lambda}\,x),
	& 0\le x\le\dfrac1n,\\[2mm]
	\displaystyle
	\left(
	\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
	\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
	\sin^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}
	\left[
	\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\sqrt{\lambda}\,
	(b_{\lambda,n}-x)
	\right],
	& \dfrac1n\le x\le b_{\lambda,n},\\[3mm]
	0,
	& b_{\lambda,n}\le x\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and it is extended evenly to $(-1,0)$. Moreover,
\[
A_{\lambda,n}
=
\|u_{\lambda,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)}
=
\left(
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{n}\right).
\]
For each fixed $n$, the mapping $\lambda\longmapsto A_{\lambda,n}$
is strictly decreasing on $(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$, and
$A_{\lambda,n}\longrightarrow0\hbox{ as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_n^*$. If
\[
A_n:=\|u_{c,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)},
\]
then
\[
A_n=
\left[
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\left(
(1-\alpha)+\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right)^2
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{n(1-\alpha)+(1+\alpha)}
\right),
\]
and
\[
\lambda_{c,n}\uparrow
\lambda_{c,\infty}:=
\frac{\pi^2}{(1-\alpha)^2},
\]
while
\[
A_n\longrightarrow
A_\infty:=
\left[
\frac{2(1-\alpha)^2}
{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
>0.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\frac{\lambda_{c,n}}{\lambda_n^*}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover, $H_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})=M_n(u_{\lambda,n})<0$, and therefore
$E_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})>0,\ E_\lambda''(u_{\lambda,n})<0$. Thus, these
explicit solutions have the variational character of the
branch $u_{\lambda,n}^-$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.219598+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0afdbdc971c547695c9e078780fb9154254908c50aad10fa4c595f8a18883c32","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\sX$ with  $\overline B\subsetneq \sX.$
 For an open subset $U\subset B,$
  we say $G^B_U(x, y)$ is
the Green function of $X^B$ in $U$ (or equivalently $X^U$)  with respect to the measure $m_B$ if it is  not identically infinite and is  the potential kernel of $X^B$ in $U$. That is, the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[\rm (i)]
 For any Borel bounded function  $f\geq 0$ on $U$,
$$
\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X_s) ds=\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X^B_s) ds = \int_U G^B_U (x, y) f(y) m_B(dy), \quad \hbox{for} \quad x\in U.
$$

\item[\rm (ii)]
For each fixed $y\in U,$ $x\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $X^B$ in $U.$ For each fixed $x\in U,$  $y\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $\wh X^{B, U}.$

 \end{enumerate}

  When   $U=B$,  we denote the Green function $G^B_U(x, y)$ by $G^B(x, y)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:20:15.584552+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b1191ef09950f6ad3cb62bb13960127422f720ada59bb83e0e3f4b160c62b41","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:scaled-murmuration of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $k\geq 2$ be fixed.  Let $P\neq 2$ be a prime, and suppose that $P$, $X$, and $Y$ tend to infinity.

{"assumptions":["X compact, T continuous.","The two limits in eps are monotone so they exist in [0, infinity];","separated and spanning counts interleave by r(n,eps) <= s(n,eps) <= r(n, eps/2), which is why the two definitions agree."],"created_at":"2026-09-12T14:04:29.025418+00:00","domain":"dynamical systems, entropy","id":"claim_0b2a19515f9b50a6070dee1dd7534cd4a246344088b2dfd716b30980eb13ccc5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. Define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max over 0 <= k < n of d(T^k x, T^k y). A set E is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if distinct points of E are at d_n-distance greater than eps; a set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if every point of X is within d_n-distance eps of some point of F. Let s(n,eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n,eps)-separated set and r(n,eps) the smallest cardinality of an (n,eps)-spanning set. Then the topological entropy is h_top(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log s(n,eps) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r(n,eps), and this agrees with the open-cover definition of Adler, Konheim and McAndrew. The quantity does not depend on the metric, only on the topology, and is invariant under topological conjugacy.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:20:07.894149+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b2a637fb99f9bae87ccc005dd98fb1ea111fd8fcbee067b2e1bcaac567e6a2f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma sylvester_equation_weight_operator of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$.

    For $i \in [\max \left( d_1 , d_2 \right)]$,
    set
    $\lambda_i := \max \left( \sigma_i, \varepsilon \right)$ with the convention of $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i > d$.
    Define the vectors
    $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1 := (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_1}) \in \R^{d_1}$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-11-02T23:06:16.394829+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_0b55c2d88e03d2f8000ab6cf220ac242624096435ae66578a4f66109c1b2ba36","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A Levy random drift destroys compactness for every confining power (2026). Let V be a two-sided semi-selfsimilar Levy process of index alpha in (0,2) and L^{w+V} = (1/2)(Delta - grad(w+V).grad) on L^2(R; e^{-(w+V)} dx), with w_1 = |x|^delta and w_2 = -|x|^delta; the unperturbed semigroups are compact exactly when delta > 1. Shiozawa and Wang (arXiv:2607.07410, Proposition 5.2) proved the perturbed semigroups noncompact for delta <= 1/alpha and left delta > 1/alpha open (their Remark 5.3(ii)). For delta > 1/alpha: if the Levy measure of V on one of the two half-lines charges (-infinity,0), the bottom of the essential spectrum of -L^{w_1+V} is 0 almost surely, and if one charges (0,infinity) the same holds for -L^{w_2+V}; in either case the semigroup is noncompact. If V changes sign and either alpha < 1 or the jumps go both ways (for instance V symmetric), both semigroups are noncompact for every delta > 0. The case alpha in [1,2) with both Levy measures on the same half-line is left open for one of the two operators. The proof uses test functions with disjoint supports around large jumps of V. {"assumptions":["Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0064-infrared-bound-for-nearest-neighbour-percolation-in-every-dimension-d","No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:26:45.042777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b65f9440e44a1939a7c37c4a3d79566b822d1d97ca4449343b4b1d8ecf71796","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine the small parameter of the lace expansion and whether a different expansion parameter exists for d in {7,...,10}. Result: The lace expansion converges when the triangle diagram at p_c is small, which for nearest-neighbour percolation is controlled by the random-walk quantities: the triangle at p_c is bounded by a constant times (2d)^{-1} times sum over n of the return probabilities, i.e. by beta_d = O(1/d); the NoBLE refinement replaces 1/d by a numerically computed constant and the bootstrap closes for d >= 11 because the computed bound on the triangle at d = 10 exceeds the threshold. Below d = 11 there is no small parameter: the triangle diagram is of order 1 but finite for d > 6, and finiteness alone does not make the expansion converge; convergence needs smallness. An alternative is to bootstrap from d = 11 downward using a continuous interpolation in the dimension (long-range or spread-out interpolation), but the interpolated models at d = 10 are spread-out models, whose infrared bound is already known, and the interpolation does not return to the nearest-neighbour model at d = 10 without passing through a non-small regime. So the obstruction is structural: the method requires a small parameter and there is none for nearest-neighbour d in {7,...,10}. A rigorous partial statement: the infrared bound holds for the nearest-neighbour model in d in {7,...,10} on any lattice whose triangle diagram at p_c is below the NoBLE threshold, which fails for Z^d but holds for some non-Z^d lattices of higher coordination number (e.g. the body-centred or the D_d-type lattices in d = 7, 8 where the coordination number is larger); I did not verify the threshold numerically for those lattices. Obstruction: No small parameter for nearest-neighbour Z^d with 7 <= d <= 10.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.580584+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0b8185d657d046e082a7b6c18e617f82ef2c43b55fb618f9ff5d5ee03cb237cf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 20 (Girsanov is not tight) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}$ and $\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}$ be the laws of the full and the directed (single-parent-conditioned) systems on a time interval $[0,\tau]$. The Radon--Nikodym density is
\[
\log\frac{d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}}{d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}}=\int_0^\tau\langle b^{-1}\Delta_t,dW_t\rangle-\frac12\int_0^\tau\|b^{-1}\Delta_t\|^2\,dt,
\]
where $\Delta_t=\gamma\,\sigma\big(s^{(v)}_t-\theta_{vu}\big)$ is the back-reaction drift. On the cascade timescale $\|\Delta_t\|=\Theta(1)$ whenever the child is active, so the quadratic-variation term is $\Theta(\tau)$ and the density is not tight toward $1$ as $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$. Hence Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red} cannot be obtained by a change of measure showing $d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}/d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}\to1$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.527213+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bb8e071126343b77b34535612ee300a284954dd91f4b90b2d41362908fc0d9e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 5 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Define
    $$ l_{1} = \max \big\{ k -j \ : \ 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k) \big\}. $$
This is the maximum length of loops in $\lambda$. Among the pairs $(j,k)$ that attain the maximum on the right-hand side of the definition of $l_{1}$ above, let $(j_{1},k_{1})$ be the one with the smallest $j$:
\begin{itemize}
\item let 
$$\Lambda (1) = \Big\{ (j, k) \, : \, 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k), \ \ k-j = l_{1} \Big\},$$
\item set 
$$ j_{1} = \min \big\{ 0 \le  j \le m \, : \, \exists k \in [j, m] \, \text{ such that } \, (j,k) \in \Lambda (1) \big\},$$
\item choose $k_{1}$ so that 
$(j_{1}, k_{1}) \in \Lambda (1). $
\end{itemize}
That is, $(j_{1},k_{1})$ is the leftmost pair $(j,k)$ such that $\lambda(j)=\lambda(k)$ and $k-j=l_{1}$.

\item[(ii)]
 We define $\lambda_{1}$ to be the path obtained from $\lambda$ by removing this maximal loop. That is, $\lambda_{1}$ is a path of length $m - k_{1} + j_{1}$ defined by 
$$ \lambda_{1} = [\lambda (0), \cdots, \lambda (j_{1}), \lambda (k_{1} +1), \cdots \lambda (m) ] = \lambda [0, j_{1}] \oplus \lambda [k_{1}, m]. $$
Note that $\lambda = \lambda_{1}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a simple path. For notational convenience, we abbreviate $\lambda$ as $\lambda_0$.

\item[(iii)] Apply the procedures (i) and (ii) above to $\lambda_{1}$ in the same way. Denote the resulting path by $\lambda_{2}$. Repeating the same procedure, $\lambda_{3}, \lambda_{4}, \cdots$ are obtained.

\item[(iv)] Define $q$ by
$$ q = \min \Big\{ l \ge 0 \ : \ \text{ $\lambda_{l}$ is a simple path} \Big\}.$$
 The largest-loop-first (LLF) loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by 
 $$ \text{LE}^{\ast} (\lambda) = \lambda_{q}. $$

\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.830532+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0bbb7013515d9200ad03b39966477906154d5f6ff3db149169d3a5bb1e6f889b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 24 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$.

Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,  we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$.

Then, for every character $(\chi, t)$ of the group $(M \times \bb R)/ M_1^{\mu}$, the operator $P_{\mu, \chi, it}$

Let $\hat{\bx} = N^{1/2} \bar{\bx}  / \|\bar{\bx}\|$ (we set this arbitrarily to $\bone \in \R^N$ if $\bar{\bx} = \bzero$). Let $\bXi'$ be an independent copy of $\bXi$ and $\hat{\by}' = \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi')$. Then
    \beq
        
        \lt|\frac{\|\hat{\by}\|^2}{N} - 1\rt|\,,
        \frac{|(\hat{\bx},\hat{\by})|}{N},
        \frac{|(\hat{\by},\hat{\by}')|}{N} \le \delta
    \eeq
   with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.

\begin{proof}
    Since $\bG \mapsto \|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $\|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $O(1)$-subgaussian by gaussian concentration of measure.
    Combined with $\E \|\bar{\bx}\|^2 = N$ this implies \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}.
    We next argue that the function
    \[
        f(\bG) = \E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}
    \]
    is also $L$-Lipschitz. Indeed,
    \[
        \nabla f(\bG)
        = \frac{\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi))(\bG,\bXi) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}}\,,
    \]
    and thus
    \[
        \|\nabla f(\bG)\|^2
        = \frac{\|\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]\|^2}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le \frac{\E[ \|\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|_\op^2 \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le L^2\,.
    \]
    Thus $\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}$ is also $O(1)$-subgaussian.
    Combined with $\E \|\hat{\by}\|^2 = N$ this proves \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc}. 
    The first inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly to \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}, applying gaussian concentration on $\bXi$ conditional on $\bG$.
    The second inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} holds by gaussian concentration because $\bXi \mapsto (\hat{\bx},\hat{\by}) / N$ is $L/N^{1/2}$-Lipschitz and $\E[\hat{\by} | \bG] = \bzero$. 
    The third inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly, conditioning further on a realization of $\hat{\by}$ such that $\|\hat{\by}\| \le 2N^{1/2}$ (which holds with probability $1-e^{-cN}$).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:29:21.917044+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c01392a1bd9c746e686d9a5483d0fcac5dfd5992ca13f504729f5d405f12239","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Extended mapping) of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $d\in\mathbb N$,
and let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\colon \mathbb R^n\to \mathbb R^k$ be a measurable mapping
such that
\[
0<\sigma_{f_j}^2:=\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)<\infty
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Let
\[
\hat f_j
=
\sigma_{f_j}^{-1}
\biggl(f_j-\int_{\mathbb R^n} f_j\,d\mu\biggr)
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},
\]
and set
$\hat f:=(\hat f_1,\ldots,\hat f_k)$.
Assume also that
\[
\hat f^{\mathbf m}:=\hat f_1^{m_1}\ldots \hat f_k^{m_k}\in L^2(\mu)
\quad \forall \mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_k)\in\mathbb Z_+^k
\quad\text{with}\quad
1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}.
\]
We define the \emph{extended mapping} of order $d$ by
\[
F_\mu^d(f)
=
\bigl(\hat f^{\mathbf m}\bigr)_{1\le |\mathbf m|\le d^{k-1}},
\]
and set
\[
\Sigma_\mu^d(f):=\operatorname{Cov}_\mu \bigl(F_\mu^d(f)\bigr).
\]
In other words, $\Sigma_\mu^d(f)$ is the matrix, in the monomial basis, of the quadratic form
\[
Q\mapsto \operatorname{Var}_\mu\bigl(Q(\hat f)\bigr),\quad Q\in\mathcal P_{d^{k-1}}(\mathbb R^k),\quad
Q(0)=0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f in L^1(mu); the conclusion fails for f merely locally integrable with a non-integrable singularity"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751760+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_0c039b146bde482b5bfdfebdcb4b9034381228ac2f84c60709b2e4ec59f3f350","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be in L^1(mu). For every eps > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that integral_A |f| dmu < eps whenever A is measurable with mu(A) < delta. Equivalently, the finite measure nu(A) = integral_A |f| dmu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu in the strong epsilon-delta sense, not merely in the sense that mu(A) = 0 implies nu(A) = 0. The two senses coincide for FINITE nu but not in general: with mu Lebesgue measure on (0,1) and nu(A) = integral_A dx/x, nu vanishes on mu-null sets yet nu(0, delta) = infinity for every delta. A single integrable function is therefore automatically a uniformly integrable family of one element. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 3.5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:41:28.174635+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c35550cf060e96c87d327a5d75e013303d61d7023ea5d49163b66c6ccdf2f10","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Tree number of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] The tree number $\tau(C)$

if $C$ is formed by merging some $C_1,\ldots,C_h$
with $H_j^*$, we let $\tau(C)=\sum_{i=1}^h\tau(C_i)+\tau_j$, where 
 $\tau_j$ is the number of tree parts
in the various $C_i$

When such a tree part $T$ is
added to $B$, we say that 
it has become {\it compromised}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.520126+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c4a826d9945f37613c92593e74bc9ccf009249296058d6b7d1cc5526420629a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:LBJ-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.","status":"unverified"}

\item For each $k\in\N$, $0$ belongs to the support of the measure $(\bfh^{(k)}|_{U_{\lm_k}^{(n_k)}})_*(\mu|_{U_{\lm_k}^{(n_k)}})$ on $\R^d$.
\item For each $i,j=1,2,\dots,d$, the measure $(\a_k\bfh^{(k)}|_{U_{\lm_k}^{(n_k)}})_*(e_k^2|\nu_{h_i^{(k)},h_j^{(k)}}|)$ converges weakly to
\[
\begin{cases}
\xi(x)\,\cL^d(dx)& (i=j)\\
0 &(i\ne j)

\]
as $k\to\infty$ for some $\xi\in L^1(\R^d,\cL^d)$ (independent of $i$) with $\sqrt{\xi}\in W^{1,2}(\R^d)$.
\item The measure $(\a_k\bfh^{(k)}|_{U_{\lm_k}^{(n_k)}})_*(\a_k^{-2}\nu_{e_k})$ on $\R^d$ converges weakly to some finite Borel measure $\rho$ as $k\to\infty$.

\a_k&=\Biggl(\muesssup_{U_{\lm_k}^{(n_k)}}|\bfh^{(k)}|\Biggr)^{-1},\\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:37:20.370993+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c5a051b9b32a1499e66a3070cc52b2c35f16c4bab7659dcda3f2d5cba581f4b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2periodic of arXiv:2411.13465, 'Height-offset variables and pinning at infinity for gradient Gibbs measures on trees'] \mbox{}\\
Let $Q: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ be a positive symmetric transfer operator of gradient type such that $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{N}}j^2 Q(j) < \infty$.
Let $\bar{\mu}$ be any (not necessarily spatially homogeneous) tree-indexed Markov chain Gibbs measure for the Ising model with interaction described by $\bar{Q}$ (see Eq. (equation eq: barQ def of the paper)). Then the following holds true for the gradient Gibbs measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$ of height-period $2$ associated to $\bar{\mu}$ on the $d$-regular tree with $d \geq 2$ via Definition (def: 2perGGM of the paper).
 \begin{itemize}
	\item[a)]\textbf{Existence.}\hypertarget{res: existence 2per}{}  Let $(H_r)_{r \in \mathbb{N}}$ be as in Definition (def: SphericalAverage of the paper). Then $H:=\lim_{r \rightarrow \infty}H_r$ is a HOV for the measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$ where the limit holds almost surely and in $\mathcal{L}^2$ with respect to the same measure $\nu^{\bar{\mu}} \circ \left(\sigma^{\rho,0} \right)^{-1}$. In particular, the measure $\mu^H$ associated with $H$ and $\nu$ via Theorem (thm: DLR of the paper) is a proper Gibbs measure on the space of height configurations. 
 \item[b1)]\textbf{Regularity of density of HOV.}\hypertarget{res: regularity density 2per}{} The corresponding distribution of $H^{\rho,0}$ obtained from Definition (def: SphericalAverage of the paper), under $\nu^{\bar{\mu}}$, has an infinitely often differentiable Lebesgue-density $f_{H^{\rho,0}}$. \\
 Moreover, $f_{H^{\rho,0}}$ is strictly positive on $\mathbb{R}$.
 \item[b2)]\textbf{Localization of single-site marginal of pinned measure.}\hypertarget{res: localization 2per}{} 
 Assume furthermore on the interaction $Q$ that there is some $R>0$ such that the function $t \mapsto \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}}\exp(tj)\frac{Q(j)}{\Vert Q \Vert_1}$ is finite for $t \in (-R,+R)$.
 Then, for every $A < (d+1)R$ there exists a $B(A) \in (0,\infty)$ such that the single site marginal at the root satisfies the following exponential decay:
 \[\mu^H(\vert \sigma_\rho \vert \geq s) \leq B(A)\exp(-As), \quad \text{for every } s \in \mathbb{N}.\]
  \item[c1)]\textbf{Peculiarity 1.}\hypertarget{res: peculiarity 1 2per}{} The lifted Gibbs measure $\mu^H$ is necessarily not invariant under the translations of the tree.
 \item[c2)]\textbf{Peculiarity 2.}\hypertarget{res: peculiarity 2 2per}{} The measure $\mu^H$
 
is not extreme in the set of all Gibbs measures for $Q$.
 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:12:46.881437+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c66c9e1a29fa27b88003aae6d0025b6ee5dfc23df8c779c9e67ec2439fa2483","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:critical-Ising of arXiv:2608.09729, 'On the self-intersection time of non-backtracking random walks'] Fix $\Delta \geq 3$ and let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex $\Delta$-regular graph.
Let $\mu$ be the Gibbs distribution of the Ising model on $G$ at inverse temperature $\beta$ satisfying $|\beta|=\beta_c$, where
\[
(\Delta-1)\tanh\beta_c=1.
\]
Then, for every $\Lambda\subseteq V(G)$, every feasible pinning $\tau\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Lambda}$, and every $u\in V(G)\setminus\Lambda$, the total influence of $u$ in $\mu^\tau$ satisfies
\[
\mathrm{TI}^{\mu^\tau}_u\le \frac{\Delta}{\Delta-1}\mathbb{E}(T(G,u))=O_\Delta(\sqrt{n}\log n).
\]
In particular, the Ising model is $O_\Delta(\sqrt{n}\log n)$-spectrally independent.

Moreover, if the external field satisfies $\|\boldsymbol h\|_\infty \le n^{O(1)}$, then the Glauber dynamics for $\mu$ has mixing time 
$\widetilde{O}_\Delta\!\left(n^{2+ \frac{2}{\Delta - 2}}\right)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.865392+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0c90623a85386cafae17fbdbeb9b5c6117edf3092c478ed32f754b9ca62db858","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 1 ($(p,n)$-proofreaders) of arXiv:2506.11358, 'Cardinalities in proofreading'] A~$(p,n)$-proofreader $\mathcal{P}$ is the pair $\mathcal{P}=
(P,\overline{s})$ with the following components which are uniquely 
determined by $p$ and $n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P=P(\overline{a},\overline{b})\cc B_n\times B_n\to B_n$ is a~map given by
$$
P(\overline{a},\,\overline{b})=
(\overline{a}_1\overline{b}_1,\,\overline{a}_2\overline{b}_2,\,\ds,\,\overline{a}_n\overline{b}_n)\,.
$$
\item The $N$-tuple of $n$-tuples
$$
\overline{s}=(\overline{s}_1,\,\overline{s}_2,\,
\ds,\,\overline{s}_N)\,, 
$$
where $\overline{s}_j\in B_n$ and $N=l^n$, is defined as follows. We 
begin with the map $f\cc[l]\to\{0,1\}$ given 
by $f(x)=1$ for $x\in[k]$ and $f(x)=0$ for $x\in[l]\setminus[k]$.
We extend it to the map $f\cc[l]^n\to B_n$ by
$$
f(a_1,\,a_2,\,\ds,\,a_n)=
(f(a_1),\,f(a_2),\,\ds,\,f(a_n))\,.
$$
We take the lexicographic ordering 
$\overline{u}_1$, $\overline{u}_2$, $\ds$, $\overline{u}_N$ of $[l]^n$, so that $\overline{u}_1=(1,1,\ds,1)$, $\overline{u}_2=
(1,1,\ds,1,2)$, $\ds$, $\overline{u}_N=(l,l,\ds,l)$. Finally, we set
$$
\overline{s}=(\overline{s}_1,\,\overline{s}_2,\,\ds,\,\overline{s}_N)=
(f(\overline{u}_1),\,f(\overline{u}_2),\,\ds,\,f(\overline{u}_N))\,.
$$
We call the $N$-tuple $\overline{s}$ the runs of $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu has compact support of positive diameter D.","t>D^2.","The source's kernel-level criterion for free Brownian unimodality."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.365295+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0ca5188ff0c8e88bf00b55cc6acb52134e15e6f99743df668c6f966aee5a39ec","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] This is the upper bound in the campaign answer to Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution. For t>0 let S(0,t) be the centered semicircle law of variance t, with density sqrt(4t-x^2)/(2pi t) on |x|<=2sqrt(t). Let mu be compactly supported with positive diameter D=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}. Then mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=D^2. Proof route: by the source's Lemma 3.1 (Biane's description), non-unimodality at time t gives some R>0 and a separating local minimum u_0 of xi_R with xi_R(u_0)<=1/t. The stationary-kernel lower bound, rescaled to diameter D, gives xi_R(u_0)>=1/D^2, so t<=D^2. At t=D^2, equality would hold in that lower bound. This forces mu to be the symmetric two-point law with atoms at u_0±D/2 and R^2=3D^2/4, which is unimodal at t=D^2 by the source's Example 2.1. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:18:19.413506+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cb2cf0faead849e90be07d57be2f3c8a4e494fce23a8f5171c4a3b58663900c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:qRacah_kernel_OPE of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] [{[mehta2004random], [Konig2005]}]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.241221+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_0cf57756fb303fe51c5a78510ee0ea2f61720aa84ba675a3743fecea3bf9f10c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (local existence and uniqueness below the classical threshold) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Fix $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$. Let $n\ge2$, let $\frac{n+1}2<s\le\frac n2+1$, let
$\Bzero\equiv\Binf\in\Rn\setminus\{0\}$, and let $v_0\in H^{s}(\Rn)$ be divergence-free. There are
constants $C\ge1$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, depending only on
$n,s,\breg$ and $v_{\rm A}$, and there exist a time $T_*>0$, a distributional
solution $(v,B, p)$ of \eqref{eq:mhd} on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ with data
$(v_0,\Binf)$, with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item writing $b:=B-\Binf$, the fields $v$, $b$ and $p$ lie in
$C([0,T_*],H^{s}(\Rn))$. The pressure is normalised by
\[
 p=\Riesz_i\Riesz_j
 \big(v^iv^j-\Binf^ib^j-b^i\Binf^j-b^ib^j\big),
\]
where $\Riesz_i$ are the Euclidean Riesz transforms;
\item writing $X=\mathrm{id}+w$, the solution is carried by a Lagrangian flow
$X:[0,T_*]\times\Rn\to\Rn$ with $X(0,\cdot)=\mathrm{id}$, uniformly bi-Lipschitz
and volume-preserving, $\det dX\equiv1$, such that $v=(\partial_tX)\circ X^{-1}$ and
$B=(\mathcal BX)\circ X^{-1}$;
moreover there is a spatially exact spacetime field
$\Ufield\in H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}(\Rst)$ such that
$\Ufield=dw$ on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$ and, for constants fixed by
the standing parameters (one may take $C=2C_{\rm lin}$, with $C_{\rm lin}$
the constant of the linear estimate \eqref{eq:linear}),
\begin{equation}
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1}_{\breg}}
 \le C\|v_0\|_{H^s},
 \qquad
 \sup_{t\in[0,T_*]}\|dw(t)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le\delta;
\end{equation}
here $\delta$ is chosen so that the second bound implies
$\|dw\|_{L^\infty_{t,y}}\le\frac12$;
\item the renormalised energy $E$ and cross helicity $H_{\rm c}$ of \eqref{eq:energy} are
conserved on $[0,T_*]$;
\item the solution is unique among all distributional solutions with the same
initial data for which $v$ and $B-\Binf$ belong to
$C([0,T_*],H^s)$. 
\end{enumerate}
The existence time is governed by the longitudinal regularity of the datum. We
distinguish the following two regimes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{\emph{(R1)}}]  $T_*$ depends on $n,s,\breg,
v_{\rm A}$, on $\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}$ and on the function
$T\mapsto\omega_{v_0}(T)$ defined in \eqref{eq:datum-modulus}.
\item[\textbf{\emph{(R2)}}] If $\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}<\infty$
for some $\rpar\in(0,1]$, then $T_*$ depends on $n,s,\breg,\rpar,v_{\rm A}$
and on $\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}+\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}$ alone. Moreover,
the spacetime field in~(2) satisfies
\[
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1+\rpar}_{\breg}}
 \le C\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

For every integer m>=1, let rho=1-m^(-2), Y=[[1,rho],[rho,1]], b(t)=(1/(2m)+t)(1,-1)^T, and G(t)=[[Y,b(t)],[b(t)^T,1]], for 0<=t<=1/(8m). Every G(t) is positive definite of rank 3 with unit diagonal.
