{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:30:36.754536+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4bfae1048e09d9f51cabc0ff101cf28990f5b6dc711cd87a6c787c074ea9e4fe","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha > \frac{6}{3-2r}$. For a sequence of inverse temperatures $\beta_N$,  the log-partition function $\ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega)$ exhibits the following two limit behaviors:

\noindent
\textbf{(a)} 
If $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to \beta \in (0, \infty)$ as $N \to \infty$, then the log-partition function centered by its multi-order polynomial drift converges in distribution to the logarithm of the continuous Wiener chaos:
$$
    \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{\lfloor 2/H \rfloor} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \stackrel{D}{\Longrightarrow} \ln Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(1, \cdot),
$$
where $Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(t, \cdot)$ is the unique solution to the following stochastic heat equation (SHE)
$$
    \partial_t u = \frac{1}{2} \Delta u + \sqrt{2}\beta u \dot{W}, \quad u(0,x) = \delta_0(x),
$$
driven by a centered Gaussian space-time noise $\dot{W}$ with covariance structure
$$
    \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\dot{W}(t,x) \dot{W}(s,y)] = H(2H-1)\delta(t-s) |x-y|^{2H-2}.
$$

\noindent
\textbf{(b)} 
Let $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$, and there exists a constant $a$ with $0 < a < A_{*}(\alpha, H)$, which is defined in \eqref{A_alpha_H}, such that 
\[
\beta_N N^{H/2} \gg N^{-a}.
\]
Then the normalized fluctuation converges to a Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right) \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where $p'=\left\lfloor\frac2H\right\rfloor$. \(\text{More generally, \(p'\) can be replaced by any integer }
p\le \lfloor2/H\rfloor
\text{ such that }
\frac{N\beta_N^{p+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\to0.\) The variance is given by
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt,
$$
with $\rho(t,x)$ being the standard heat kernel. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-02T01:20:52.931336+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2605.24611, 2026): owner_math","id":"claim_4bfb4312751e7b4b65a99c25a8bda6a321b048b42ff129e2faf2efae009dfffa","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 (Limit cycle and basin of attraction) of arXiv:2605.24611, 'Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks'] A limit cycle of period P ≥1 is a set of distinct states C = {x(0), x(1), . . . , x(P −1)} such that, for the synchronous update map F : {−1, 1}n → {−1, 1}n, we have F(x(i)) = x(i+1) for i = 0, . . . , P −2 and F(x(P −1)) = x(0). Clearly, C ⊆B(C); we call C a limit-cycle attractor if C ⊊B(C).","status":"unverified"}

The proposition that such cardinals exist cannot be proved in the most common axiomatization of set theory, namely ZFC, and such propositions can be viewed as ways of measuring how \"much\", beyond ZFC, one needs to assume to be able to prove certain desired results. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.142700+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c46c6a1dbe7ddf1cd9704d0a1a1e438449cf0a0452e6aa8850046fbeeae9192","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:three-causes of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] For a nonnegative supermartingale $(M_n)$ with $M_0=1$ crossing the level $b>1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The martingale-versus-supermartingale gap governs $D_b$. If $(M_n)$ is a martingale then $\delta_n\equiv0$ and $D_b=0$; the loss term is nonzero precisely to the extent that the process is a strict supermartingale, that is, sheds predictable mass before crossing.
\item Bounded overshoot governs $O_b$. If the conditional landing value satisfies $\mathbb{E}[M_{T_b}\mid \mathcal{F}_{T_b-1},T_b=n]\le b+\omega$ a.s. for a constant $\omega$, then $O_b\le\omega$ ((sec:overshoot of the paper)); on a lattice that includes $b$, $O_b=0$. The overshoot is nonzero precisely to the extent that the increments can carry the process strictly past the boundary.
\item Wobbling governs $R_b$. If, in the martingale case, conditions (i)--(ii) of (thm:wobbling of the paper) hold (sufficient wobbling and bounded overshoot), then $\mathbb{P}(T_b<\infty)=1$, so the survival event is null and $R_b=0$. The residual is nonzero precisely to the extent that wobbling fails -- that is, to the extent that paths can settle and survive forever without crossing.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:35:04.197884+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c63e8b305c62e41b425da64218ae3cbde2f819431e38f13b4a00ad4ef070029","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] \phantomsection

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If the nested fractal graph is \(h\)-flexible,
then
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h}}{c_n}=\mu^h.
  
\end{equation}
In particular, \(1\)-flexibility implies
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\mu.
\]
\item For the regular polygonal \(N\)-gasket with \(N\ge3\) and
\(4\nmid N\), write
\[
  N=4k_N+\ell_N,\qquad
  \ell_N\in\{1,2,3\},\qquad
  s_N=k_N+1,
\]
and put
\[
  h_N
  =
  \gcd\bigl(N-2s_N,\,2s_N-(N-2s_N)\bigr).
\]
Then \(h_N\) is the smallest flexibility step.  In fact, the graph is
\(h_N\)-flexible at scale \(2\), and
\[
  h_N=
  \begin{cases}
    2,&N\equiv2\pmod4,\\
    3,&N\equiv9\pmod{12},\\
    1,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h_N}}{c_n}=\mu_N^{h_N}.
\]
\item The standard Vicsek graph is not \(h\)-flexible for any
\(h\ge1\).  Its connective constant is
\(\mu=\sqrt2\), but, for every \(k\ge2\),
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  c_{3^k-2}&=2^{(3^k+1)/2},\\
  c_{3^k-1}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-3)/2},\\
  c_{3^k}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-1)/2}.
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \frac{c_{3^k-1}}{c_{3^k-2}}=\frac34,
  \qquad
  \frac{c_{3^k}}{c_{3^k-1}}=2,
\]
and the successive ratios do not converge.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

When \(0\leq a<1<b\), let \(\tau(a,b)\) be the larger root of
\[
t^2-b(1+a)t+ab=0.
\]
Define \(K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}\colon[0,\infty)^2\to[0,1]\) by
\[
K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}(a,b)
=
\begin{cases}
1,
& b\leq 1,\\
\frac{2}{\tau(a,b)}-\frac{1}{\tau(a,b)^2},
& 0\leq a<1<b,\\
\frac{1}{ab},
& 1\leq a.
\end{cases}
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:31:20.615284+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4c6c543f211775f81e17258e84be6b56ba7c5c724d2ea53c655e440161959d78","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $(S,\mathcal{E})$ and $(T,\mathcal{F})$ be coarse spaces.
A map $f : S \rightarrow T$ is called: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \emph{controlled} (cf.~\cite{BunkeEngel2020}) if, for each $E\in \mathcal{E}$, 
    \[
    \Ad_f(E) = \{ (f(x_1),f(x_2)) \mid (x_1,x_2) \in E \} \subset T \times T
    \]
    is an entourage on $T$, 
    \item  \emph{coarsely proper} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if the set $f^\dagger[D]=f^{-1}(D)$ is bounded in $S$ for any bounded subset $D$ of $T$,  
    \item \emph{coarse} (cf.~\cite{Roe2003LectureCoarse}) if it is controlled and coarsely proper,
    \item  \emph{effectively proper} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if, for any $F\in \mathcal{F}$, the relation 
    \[
    \Ad_{f^\dagger}F = \{ (p,q) \mid (f(p),f(q)) \in F \} \subset S \times S
    \]
    is also an entourage on $S$,
    \item   \emph{a coarse embedding} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if $f$ is controlled and effectively proper,
    \item  \emph{coarsely surjective} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if there exists $F\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $F[f(S)] = T$,
    \item  \emph{a coarse equivalence} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZava2017}) if $f$ is controlled and there exists a controlled map $h: T\to S$ such that $h\circ f\sim \id_S$ and $f\circ h\sim \id_T$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

Theory Related Fields 160 (2014), Problem 7.5) asked whether, for every process X whose law is equivalent to Wiener measure, a random piece of path can be put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion. The paper proves that absolute continuity with respect to Wiener measure is enough: on an extension of the probability space there are a standard Brownian motion B and an almost surely finite random integer N >= 0 with X_t = B_{N+t} - B_N for all t >= 0; N cannot in general be a stopping time for B. The construction is Rost's filling scheme (Chacon-Ornstein, Rost 1971) for the unit shift of two-sided Brownian motion. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.207864+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cd786f90401a1fa66a664ea5f8dc03669df306bc70c61300bf3f74e7013f574","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi Def:W-homotopy-Equiv of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Let $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ be 
    weighted polyhedra of the same type and
       $f, g: (X,\lambda)\rightarrow (X',\lambda')$ be two  
     W-continuous maps. A \emph{W-homotopy} from $f$ to $g$ relative
to $A\subseteq X$ is a W-continuous map
$$H : (X \times [0, 1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1}) \rightarrow (X',\lambda')$$ which satisfies:
 \begin{itemize}
   \item $H(x, 0) =f(x)$ and $H(x,1)=g(x)$ for all $x\in X$;\vskip 0.1cm
   \item $H(a,t)=f(a)=g(a)$ for all $a\in A$ and 
   $t\in [0,1]$.\vskip 0.1cm
   \end{itemize}
   
   Here $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ is considered as a weighted polyhedron, and $(X\times [0,1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1})$ is the product $(X,\lambda)$ with
   $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$.
   \vskip 0.1cm
   If there exists a W-homotopy from $f$ to $g$,
   we say that $f$ is \emph{W-homotopic to} $g$.
   If moreover $H$ is weight-preserving, we say
   that $f$ is \emph{strongly W-homotopic to} $g$ (a priori $f$ and $g$ must be both weight-preserving).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:45:17.700349+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cd9262edc740cc64a92e63db50ae2dbcd7e78906e745abdfce808989bc1bda9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:bound_asymptotics of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] Let $\kappa_{q,k} := \log((k-3)/(1-q))$ and $u(T) := \frac{2-\exp(-T/2)}{1-\exp(-T/2)}$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:53.192689+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4cd9dd1ade8eea879b530c4cc2d3db734d279b76fb3c9c03bc426ad2deeb77e3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ be a nonempty index set with $|U|=m$ and let
$\pi_U:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{N}^m$ be the coordinate projection.
Define the projected increments $X_n^{[U]}:=\pi_U(X_n)$.
Then $(X_n^{[U]})_{n\ge 1}$ is an i.i.d.\ sequence on $\mathbb{N}^m$ with pmf

\begin{equation}
f^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{P}(X_1^{[U]}=k_U),
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m.
\end{equation}

Assume $f^{[U]}(0_m)<1$ (non-degeneracy in the projected coordinates), and define the
projected renewal chain and counting process by

\begin{equation}
S_0^{[U]}=0_m,
\qquad
S_n^{[U]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[U]},
\qquad n\ge 1,
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
N^{[U]}(k_U):=\sup\{n\in\mathbb{N}: S_n^{[U]}\le_m k_U\},
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m,
\end{equation}

where $\le_m$ denotes componentwise order in $\mathbb{N}^m$.
Its renewal function is

\begin{equation*}
M^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{E}[N^{[U]}(k_U)].
\end{equation*}

\smallskip
\noindent
In particular, for $U=\{u\}$ one recovers the univariate marginal renewal process
$S_n^{[u]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[u]}$ and the marginal counting process

$N^{[u]}(k_u)=\sup\{n:S_n^{[u]}\le k_u\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.019073+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ce3db8d352481f4241a1a20d7645ef60790d5c295ebeacf0fae7d121e465192","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T}\) be a fixed limiting point of a compact
finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow of complex dimension \(n\ge2\), and
let \((Z,d,\cR,g,J,f,\mathfrak m)\) be the time-\((-1)\) model of a
tangent space at \(\xi\).  Thus \(Z\) has
the finite-time tangent-space package of
\cref{sp:prop:limiting-package}: it is the intrinsic completion
of its K\"ahler regular locus, is normal and klt, carries the normalized
shrinker measure and complete soliton flow, and has smooth
metric--complex--density convergence and the local ambient metric lower
bound.  Let \(A\) be the nonnegative
self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of
\[
 \cE_0(\phi,\psi)=
 \int_{\cR}\langle\nabla\phi,\nabla\overline\psi\rangle\,d\mathfrak m,
 \qquad \phi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\cR).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
                     \sigma(A)\subset\{0\}\cup[1/2,\infty),
                     \qquad\ker A=\C1.
\end{equation}
If \(u:Z\to\C\) is holomorphic and globally \(d\)-Lipschitz, then
\(u\in L^2(Z,\mathfrak m)\), and
\begin{equation}
 A\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right)
 =\frac12\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
          \nabla^2\Re u=\nabla^2\Im u=0\qquad\text{on }\cR.
\end{equation}
Here \(A\) is the canonical Friedrichs form generator; no
essential-self-adjointness assertion is made for the minimal operator on
the incomplete regular locus. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:37:08.955794+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d0850de5b28c4a7bc8e53651048f9d8d7a85ebea2650c557730166733bc5f7a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:variance_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Consider the empirical density $\overline{\rho}_t(V)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and empirical current $\overline J_t(U)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper))

    &\leq \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}t},

    &\leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\E^\mu[Q]

      \leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right),

	\quad\quad

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:41:19.337998+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d0ae279897409c629da41475c691712daf1ae99de6a91cf613f42377a0bd1f9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] We have the following convergences:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The number $N^\kappa$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^\kappa_A$ converges in law to the number $N^4$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$ as $\kappa \uparrow 4$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.312734+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d2acbb248d639a1830874a0adc9e54fa44dcf374657839614b7c42d46d6d85c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma one-step-descent-convex of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, closed, convex, and bounded, and let
   $ D_{\mathcal X}:=\sup_{u,v\in\mathcal X}\|u-v\|<\infty .$
Suppose that $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth on a convex neighborhood containing the iterates and $\mathcal X$. Let
    $x^\star:=\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal X} f(x),~~
    G_\star:=\|\nabla f(x^\star)\|.$
Consider the update in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper)
with $\epsilon(1+L\eta)\le 2, \eta\mu<1.$
Assume that, for every $z$, $\widehat\pi_t(z)\in\mathcal X, \|\widehat\pi_t(z)-\pi_{\mathcal X}(z)\|\le E_t.$

    ~
    \mathcal V_t:=f(p_t)-f(x^\star)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\|p_t-x^\star\|^2.$
Define
\begin{align*}
    \rho:=1-\epsilon\eta\mu,&
    \quad
    A_{\eta,\epsilon}:=1+\epsilon\eta L,\quad 
    M_\eta:=G_\star+\left(L+\frac{1}{\eta}\right)D_{\mathcal X},
    \quad
    C_\eta:=\frac{L}{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta},\\
   & B_1:=M_\eta A_{\eta,\epsilon},

    +

    \epsilon M_\eta E_t
    +
    2\epsilon^2C_\eta E_t^2.
\end{align*}
Moreover, the normal component satisfies
   $ \|n_{t-1}\|
    \le
    (1-\epsilon)\|n_t\|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["G finite, p prime with p dividing |G|"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:31:12.478772+00:00","domain":"group theory","id":"claim_4d35593daa64c444cac9ce0985344a1fd51aea56f0ba9d34f01bd81800978194","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p, hence a subgroup of order p. More precisely (McKay), the number of solutions to x^p = e in G is a multiple of p, and since x = e is one of them, there are at least p - 1 elements of order p; in fact the number of elements of order p is congruent to -1 modulo p. Cauchy's theorem is the p^1 case of Sylow's first theorem (a subgroup of order p^a exists whenever p^a divides |G|) and is the converse of Lagrange's theorem for prime orders; the converse of Lagrange fails in general (A_4 has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:07:15.726839+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d3cf72c243ca43f0092b4a117da076edc55df97128ced7bcf0a7570584c3ed8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:vector-valued of arXiv:2608.01279, 'Stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate Hölder diffusion coefficient: uniqueness below'] Let \(d\geq1\), \(\beta\in(2/3,1)\), and let
\[
    G:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}
\]
be a measurable mapping that satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For some constant \(c_G>0\),
\[
    G(z)G(z)^{*}\geq c_G^2 I_d,
    \qquad z\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
\item    For some constant \([G]_{C^\beta}<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
    \|G(z)-G(z')\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
       \leq [G]_{C^\beta}\|z-z'\|^\beta,
    \qquad \forall z,z'\in\mathbb R^d.
    
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Consider the following vector-valued stochastic heat equation
$$
    \partial_t U
      =\Delta U+G(U)\dot W,
      \qquad
      U(0)=u_0\in L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d),
$$
where \(W=(W^1,\ldots,W^d)\) is a \(d\)-dimensional
space--time white noise.

Then weak uniqueness holds for the above equation in
$
    C\bigl([0,T];L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d)\bigr)
$
for every \(T>0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.097652+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d4bc2c914255102e0b0fa0df3fd56d972fe9eab9b698b26f4419da6aace4953","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:singleton-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For a Kac plane $i$, let
\[
 W_i^\circ=\Pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W)
\]
be its pure-Weyl coefficient.  On the common star space, with an arbitrary
passive ancillary Hilbert space $E$, put
\[
 (\mathsf M h)(i,\theta)=(W_i^\circ\otimes I_E)h(i,\theta),
 \qquad \mathsf J=\mathscr E^*\mathscr E,
 \qquad \mathsf Q=I-\mathsf J.
\]
Relative to $\operatorname{ran}\mathsf J\oplus
\operatorname{ran}\mathsf Q$, write
\[
 \mathsf M=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&\mathsf S^-\\ \mathsf S^+&\mathsf V\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.2.10n}
\]
We call $0,\mathsf S^-,\mathsf S^+,\mathsf V$ the four
\emph{star statuses} of a passive singleton; a status record chooses one
of these four blocks for every singleton after equal-time fusion.  These
statuses are distinct from the derivative-placement coefficients
$(\alpha,\beta)$ used in the Ricci root calculus.
Then
\[
 \|\mathsf S^-\|=\|\mathsf S^+\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{N(n-1)}}\le N^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\mathsf V\|\le2,
\tag{3.2.10o}
\]
and the one-sided utilized-step maps factor through the innovation:
\[
 \mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr T=\mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr G,
 \qquad
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*
 =\mathscr G^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*.
\tag{3.2.10p}
\]
Consequently a passive singleton isolated between invariant separators is
zero.  A run of $s\ge2$ passive singletons with $s-1$ prescribed finite
Green gates has norm at most
\[
 \frac{2^{2s-3}}N.
\tag{3.2.10q}
\]
Thus its two endpoints create one $N^{-1}$ resource and every interior
singleton transports that same resource; no additional token is created.
The same conclusion holds when an endpoint is a $\mathscr D$- or
$\mathscr L$-incidence, with the corresponding mixed bound of
(lem:riesz of the paper) and with the already existing root or packet token
transported.","status":"unverified"}

$\sreg\ge0$, $\preg\in\Real$ and $0<T\le1$. For every

\[

 (u,\partial_tu)|_{t=0}=(f_0,f_1),

satisfying

 \le C_{\rm lin}\Big(

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:01:48.616781+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d62894fa704ec9119436ba9f05f292e516c902eff83146ff7648ed3662d0e7a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:taylor-eta2345 of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] There exist numerical constants $c,C>0$ such that the following holds. For $2\le k\le 5$, define the functions
\begin{align*}
E_2(x_1,x_2) 
&\triangleq \zeta^2\mathsf{S}_{2,1}\,,\\
E_3(x_1,x_2,x_3)
&\triangleq (1-1/d) a\zeta^3 \mathsf{S}_{3,2}\,,\\
E_4(x_1,\ldots,x_4)

W_{hi}W_{hj}W_{uv},

\{u,v\}=[5]\setminus\{h,i,j\}\,.
\end{align*}
Define the residuals $R_k\equiv \eta_k-E_k$. On the event $a^2\delta_k \le c$,

{"assumptions":["phi_i 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0","eps_i independent Rademacher signs","T bounded so the suprema are finite; constant 1 WITHOUT absolute values, 2 WITH them"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.628629+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d71e82701baa0652e97a3150c16f319f1bfdeca9e4a8d8cfae7f2157af90f94","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let T be a bounded subset of R^n, let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent Rademacher signs, and let phi_i : R -> R be 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0 for every i. Then E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i phi_i(t_i) <= E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i t_i. With ABSOLUTE VALUES inside the supremum the same statement holds with a factor 2: E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i phi_i(t_i) | <= 2 E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i t_i |. The distinction between the constants 1 and 2 is a standard source of misquotation; the constant 1 belongs to the version WITHOUT absolute values. The hypothesis phi_i(0) = 0 is needed for the version without absolute values and can be arranged by subtracting a constant, which is harmless for a symmetric process. In statistical learning the principle is what lets one strip a Lipschitz loss off a function class without changing the Rademacher complexity by more than a constant. [Ledoux and Talagrand, Probability in Banach Spaces, Theorem 4.12]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["F entire on C (or C^d)","claims of band limitation require the growth bound off the real axis","L^2 version needs square integrability on R; distributions need the polynomial-growth version"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.264631+00:00","domain":"complex and harmonic analysis, common errors","id":"claim_4d88e0d15b6e8881d2eb18cd54107f75b8c1834afa521c13029e34cc2e348e2d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypotheses: (1) the growth bound $|F(z)|\\le Ce^{A|z|}$ must hold for all complex $z$, not merely on $\\mathbb R$; (2) $F$ must be square integrable on $\\mathbb R$ (for the $L^2$ version) or have controlled polynomial growth (for the distributional version). Failure of (1): $F(z)=e^{-z^2}$ is entire and its restriction to $\\mathbb R$ is in $L^2$, yet $|F(iy)|=e^{y^2}$, so $F$ is of order 2, not of exponential type; its Fourier transform is a Gaussian, supported everywhere - no band limitation. Failure of (2): $F(z)=\\cos(Az)$ is entire of exponential type exactly $A$ and bounded on $\\mathbb R$, but not in $L^2(\\mathbb R)$; it is not $\\int_{-A}^A\\varphi(t)e^{itz}dt$ for any $\\varphi\\in L^2$, only for the measure $\\frac12(\\delta_A+\\delta_{-A})$ - the correct statement in that regime is the Paley-Wiener-Schwartz theorem for compactly supported distributions, with a polynomial factor $(1+|\\zeta|)^N$ allowed. Similarly $F(z)=e^{Az}$ has type $A$ but grows on the real axis. Two further traps: the exponential factor in Paley-Wiener-Schwartz measures the support of the transform only through the supporting function of its convex hull, so the theorem detects $\\operatorname{ch}(\\operatorname{supp}u)$, not the support itself; and no such function can have both itself and its transform compactly supported, since a nonzero entire function cannot vanish on an open set (see Benedicks' theorem for the measure-theoretic strengthening).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.572375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4d8dd37cc870c042d2c739c5c64707ff5d28cdf721b491d658978013ec700ff6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:matrix.normal.Wishart.operator.connection of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Let $\nu\in [d, \infty)\cap \mathbb{N}$, $\Sigma\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d$, and let $f:\mathcal{S}_{++}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth. Set
\[
\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d} \vcentcolon= \{X\in \mathbb{R}^{\nu\times d}: \mathrm{rank}(X)=d\}.
\]
The set $\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$ is open, and its complement has Lebesgue measure zero. For $X\in \mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$, define $g_f(X) = f(X^{\top}X)$. Then, pointwise on $\mathcal{R}_{\nu,d}$,
\begin{equation}
\left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{OU}}g_f\right)(X) = \left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{W}}_{\nu, \Sigma} \, f\right)(X^{\top}X), \qquad X\in \mathcal{R}_{\nu,d},
\end{equation}
where $\nabla f$ denotes the symmetric gradient in the variable $S$ and
\[
\left(\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{W}}_{\nu, \Sigma} \, f\right)(S) = 2 \, \mathrm{tr}\{(\nu\Sigma - S)\nabla f(S)\} + 4 \, \mathrm{tr}\{S \nabla \Sigma \nabla f(S)\}, \qquad S\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

=

{"assumptions":["X_1, ..., X_n independent","Z = f(X) nonnegative with E[Z log Z] finite"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627951+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4dc336ffe1859932768872cd898d8a70b2b6935d4bd7b90c575ded181869d08f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) be a nonnegative random variable with E[Z log Z] finite. Write Ent(Z) = E[Z log Z] - E[Z] log E[Z] and let Ent^{(i)}(Z) denote the same functional computed with respect to X_i alone, with the other coordinates held fixed. Then Ent(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]. The same statement with variance in place of entropy is the Efron-Stein inequality, and the two are the p = 2 and p = 1 members of a family of phi-entropies that all tensorize. Tensorization is what converts a ONE-DIMENSIONAL functional inequality into an n-dimensional one with no loss of constant: if each coordinate's law satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, then the product law satisfies it with the SAME constant C, independent of n. That dimension-free feature is the whole reason the entropy method produces concentration bounds that do not degrade as n grows. Independence of the coordinates is essential. [standard; e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 4.10 and Section 4.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:41:11.635894+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4dc3f1bcec7db304a707ed1904c1873b2db694de992292bd0c81d99a5696c2e8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma terms_in_signature_first of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] \[

as required, where we use \(\xi_{0ii}=\xi_{ii0}\) (reversal property) to obtain the final equivalence.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.811654+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4de935b0a21ceccfcbfd91d058d6e45d801c271e7ed606e5a935aa06072cdef1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop ProdContSing of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathfrak{X} := V(h) \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}_\kappa^{\ell_1+\cdots + \ell_m} $,
	where
	\[
		h := \prod_{\alpha=1}^m P_{\ell_\alpha} (z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)}) + \delta 
		\in \kappa [ z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)} \mid \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \}]
	\]
	with 
	$ \delta \in \kappa $. 
	If $ \delta $ is invertible, 
	then $ \mathfrak{X} $ is singular if and only if the following two conditions hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item[(a)] 
		$ \ell_\alpha = 2 k_\alpha $ is even, 
		with $  k_\alpha \geq 1 $,
		for all $ \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \} $, and 
		
		\item[(b)] 
		$ (-1)^{k_1 + \cdots + k_m} + \delta  = 0 $.
	\end{enumerate}
	In the singular case, $ \Sing (\mathfrak{X}) $ is the origin and the hypersurface $ \mathfrak{X} $ has an isolated singularity of type $ A_1 $ at the origin. 
	\\
	On the other hand, if $ \delta = 0 $, then 
	$ \mathfrak{X} $ is a simple normal crossing divisor with $ m $ disjoint irreducible components, 
	i.e., after a suitable choice of coordinates $ h $ is of the form $ x_1 \cdots x_m $ with $ (x_1, \ldots, x_m) $ part of the chosen coordinates.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["simple random walk on the stated graphs","k -> infinity"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T02:55:51.199348+00:00","domain":"probability/random-walks/cover-time","id":"claim_4e18e3b3b9bb4458ae508a2c4b2b674e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (arXiv:1004.4371, Section 5: when t_hit = o(t_cov), are the cover-time fluctuations of order t_hit?) is answered in the negative. On the clique-star G_k (a k-clique with one pendant leaf at each clique vertex; t_hit = 2k^2 + k + 1) the cover time satisfies Var(tau_cov) ~ t_hit t_cov and (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/sqrt(Var tau_cov) converges to a standard Gaussian; on the double star D_k (two adjacent centres, each with k pendant leaves; t_hit = 6k + 3) the cover time centred at 4k log k and divided by 2 sqrt(2) k sqrt(log k) converges to |Z|, a half-normal law, with t_cov = 4k log k + (4/sqrt(pi)) k sqrt(log k) + o(k sqrt(log k)) and Var(tau_cov) = 8(1 - 2/pi) k^2 log k (1 + o(1)). Centred at its mean instead, (tau_cov - t_cov)/sqrt(t_hit t_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(3), and the standardized cover time (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/SD(tau_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(1 - 2/pi), not to a half-normal law; SD(tau_cov)/t_hit ~ (sqrt(2)/3) sqrt(1 - 2/pi) sqrt(log k) -> infinity. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.695099+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4e2841da640a398408c72f98a4c00ba304f3a51379b2beecfbd04e38294d3c1f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:whole-plane-persistence of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exists $C=C(\kappa,M,R)>0$ such that the following
holds.  For $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}\geq0,\qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^2}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf0).
\end{equation}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of the two-dimensional Euler equation in $\mathbb R^2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})^2
  \leq C\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0}).
\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\leq\frac{\kappa^2}{C},
\end{equation}
then, with
\[
  \mathbf X_\varepsilon
  :=\frac1\kappa\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathbf x
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)\,\mathrm d\mathbf x,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_\varepsilon|
  \leq (1+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b|
  \leq(2+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
In particular, for any family of initial data satisfying
(equation eq:whole-plane-initial-data of the paper) with the same $\kappa,M,R$, if
$\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, then
\[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}|\mathbf b|\longrightarrow0.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["both sequences (or functions) monotone in the same direction; opposite directions reverse the inequality","no independence or product structure needed beyond the single variable; the n-variable generalization is Harris-FKG"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049386+00:00","domain":"correlation inequalities (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_4e33e7a855f3b1ed38c5b184f81787d0bc6049fa0a51bfd8ff8f2972faba1f89","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"If a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n and b_1 >= b_2 >= ... >= b_n (both sequences sorted the same way), then (1/n) sum a_i b_i >= ((1/n) sum a_i) ((1/n) sum b_i); if one sequence is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses. The integral form: for f and g both monotone in the same direction on [0,1], the integral of f g is at least the product of the integrals. This is the one-dimensional case of the Harris-FKG inequality (a product of two increasing functions of one uniform variable has nonnegative covariance), and its proof is the identity 2(n sum a_i b_i - sum a_i sum b_j) = sum_{i,j} (a_i - a_j)(b_i - b_j) >= 0.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Y = sum_{k>=0} B_k (2/3)^k with i.i.d. digits B_k, P(B_k=1)=p (the biased-coin Bernoulli convolution at contraction ratio lambda=2/3, equivalently the same non-Pisot ratio 3/2 used elsewhere in this campaign)","elementary dimension bound only: Hochman's theorem is NOT used; only the entropy-over-Lyapunov upper bound on dimension and the fact that a measure on R of dimension below 1 cannot be absolutely continuous"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.956588+00:00","domain":"probability/Bernoulli convolutions","id":"claim_4e3f794ecd634c87b21e676f1227583d","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 - the law of sum_k B_k (2/3)^k with B_k i.i.d., P(B_k = 1) = p - the measure is singular for every p < p* = 0.140277, where p* solves H(p) = log(3/2) in natural logarithms (H(p)/log(3/2) = 0.4896, 0.8018, 1.2341, 1.7095 at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1/2). Proof: the dimension of the measure is at most the entropy-over-Lyapunov ratio H(p)/log(3/2), and a measure on the line of dimension below one is not absolutely continuous; Hochman's theorem is needed only for the matching lower bound dim = min(1, H(p)/log(3/2)), which this does not use. Two further thresholds govern the Fourier criterion at this ratio. The biased factor |(1-p) + p e^{i phi}|^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p)(1 - cos phi) has arithmetic mean 1 - 2p(1-p) over the phase, which gives the annealed (main-term) exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2), zero at p(1-p) = 1/6, i.e. p = (1 - 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.211325; and log-mean 2 log(1-p), which gives the quenched (typical) threshold (3/2)(1-p)^2 = 1 at p = 0.183503. As a calibration control for statistics on the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 2/3 (the same ratio, frequencies and arithmetic, only the weights changed): below p* the measure is singular and a detection is expected; above 0.2113 the main term decays and a pass is expected; between 0.1403 and 0.2113 the measure has dimension one while the main term already diverges, so a reading there means nothing - controls belong at p <= 0.12 and p >= 0.35. Unlike the Pisot control lambda = 1/phi, where one localised cell forces the reading a priori, the absence of such a cell at ratio 3/2 is Mahler's open problem on ||(3/2)^m xi||, so the control's genuineness rests on an empirical extensiveness test: a flat per-step rate means one cell forces the reading, a wobbling rate means a real measurement (flat to 0.0005 at 1/phi from K = 8; wobbling by 0.028 at the unbiased 2/3).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.723939+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4e92ce6e9b8fc59cb1d4748bc8c36496d4a69b015f697587300eb89a24e12c0a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $f:\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be a smooth, compactly supported function and let $\varepsilon, \tilde{\varepsilon}, \delta, \zeta\in [0,\infty)$ and $a,b, \tilde{a},\tilde{b}\in\Rsf^m$ be such that 
	\[
		|b-a|\leq \varepsilon, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a}|\leq \tilde{\varepsilon}, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{a}-a|\leq \delta, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a} - (b-a)| \leq \zeta.
	\]
Let also $T_0,T_1: \Rsf^m\times\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be defined by 
	\begin{align*}
		& T_0(x,y):= f(y)-f(x),\\
		& T_1(x,y):= f(y)-f(x)- \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^j}(x)(y^j-x^j)
	\end{align*}
for $x,y\in\Rsf^m$. Then
	\[
		\left|T_0(a,b)\right|  \lesssim \varepsilon 
		\quad\mbox{and}\quad
		|T_0(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_0(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon(\delta + \zeta) + \zeta,
	\]
and
	\[
		 |T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2
		 \quad \mbox{and}\quad 
		 |T_1(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2(\delta + \zeta) + (\varepsilon + \tilde{\varepsilon})\zeta
	\]
where the constants are non-decreasing functions of $C^1$, $C^2$, $C^2$, and $C^3$ norm of $f$, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.222512+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ec5ac7206a02ee269e114086078147bb6c150f5945dff018a8b030b50638a48","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 29 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\R^d.$
Suppose that $U$ is an open subset of $B$. A Borel function $u$ on
$B$ is said to be:
\begin{itemize}
\item harmonic in $U$ with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
\begin{equation}
u(x) = \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{V}})],\qquad
x\in V,
\end{equation}
for every bounded open set $V$ with $\overline{V}\subset U$;

\item excessive with respective to $X^{b, B}$ if $u$ is
nonnegative and for every $t > 0$ and $x\in B$
\[
u(x) \geq \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{t})]
\quad\mbox{and}\quad u(x) = \lim_{t \downarrow0}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)];
\]

\item a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if it is excessive
with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and for every sequence $\{U_n\}_{n \ge1}$
of open sets with
$\overline{U}_n \subset U_{n+1}$ and $\bigcup_n U_n = B$,
\[
\lim_{n \to\infty}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{U_n}})] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B\mbox{-a.e. } x\in B;
\]

\item a pure potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
it is a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and

\[
\lim_{t \to\infty} \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B \mbox{-a.e. } x\in B.
\]

\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:24:20.645892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4ec873d06ff22a2b37214214c7389d6627ae122b760d7d702368898982b7647c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:main1 of arXiv:2608.11084, 'Sharp Frobenius-Norm Concentration for Sample Moment Tensors'] Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and
sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge 2\) be an integer. Then, for every
\(q\ge1\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\mathbbm{E}
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}
-
\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
K^p
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
\]
where
\[
\rho_p(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2},
& p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2},
& p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, if $X$ is Gaussian, then
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbbm{E} \bigg\|
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^N
X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\asymp_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}}
+
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
\]
where
\[
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["entries independent up to symmetry with mean 0 and variance 1 before scaling by 1/sqrt n","moments bounded uniformly in n (finite fourth moment suffices for the semicircle limit of the empirical spectral distribution; the diagonal entries may have a different variance)","the moment method identifies the limit because the semicircle law is determined by its moments (compact support)"],"created_at":"2026-09-02T07:51:33.049288+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory (hand-authored statement with hypotheses, 2026-09-02)","id":"claim_4f1567c38734286426940b4f4f52f264db38c2264b6a25725643dc91aea4918c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For the semicircle density (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(4 - x^2) on [-2, 2] (mean 0, variance 1), all odd moments vanish and the 2k-th moment equals the Catalan number C_k = (1/(k+1)) binom(2k, k): 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, ... . A semicircle of radius R has 2k-th moment C_k (R/2)^{2k}. In the moment method for a Wigner matrix W = X / sqrt n, where X is real symmetric with independent entries above the diagonal, mean 0 and variance 1, the normalized traces satisfy E tr(W^{2k}) / n -> C_k: expanding the trace as a sum over closed walks of length 2k on the index set, only walks whose edges are each traversed exactly twice and whose underlying graph is a tree survive as n grows, and such walks are counted by C_k; the Catalan numbers determine the semicircle law uniquely because it has compact support. Wigner's theorem then follows from convergence of moments plus a variance bound (or a concentration bound on the trace) giving weak convergence of the empirical spectral distribution in probability.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f holomorphic on a punctured disc around a, a an isolated essential singularity","the conclusion is density, not surjectivity: Picard's great theorem is the stronger, deeper statement"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:05:27.626465+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_4f2a0d209f59418cfbe6a3e636baf86d6aab06cd28c72428263a3b5173a5e488","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f be holomorphic on a punctured disc D' = { 0 < |z - a| < r } and suppose a is an essential singularity of f (neither removable nor a pole; equivalently the Laurent series at a has infinitely many negative-power terms). Then for every 0 < rho < r the image f({ 0 < |z - a| < rho }) is dense in C: for every w in C and every eps > 0 there are points z arbitrarily close to a with |f(z) - w| < eps. Equivalently, every complex number is a limit of f along some sequence z_n -> a. The three singularity types are thereby characterised by the behaviour of |f| near a: bounded (removable, Riemann), tending to infinity (pole), neither (essential). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.844621+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4f3a76af7669e71634cef341c091b25d6e3fca816ad2d4eac83135014d29ad47","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 4 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $(\A,\tau)$ be a $W^\ast$-probability space, and let $a\in\A$ (just $L^2(\A,\tau)$ suffices).  Then $a^\ast a = |a|^2$ is selfadjoint, and so has a spectral measure $\mu_{|a|^2}$: the unique compactly-supported probability distribution on $\R_+$ whose moments are given by $\int x^k \mu_{|a|^2}(dx) = \tau[(a^\ast a)^k]$ (see \eqref{eq.spectral.meas}).  Denote by $\nu_a$ the push-forward of $\mu_{|a|^2}$ under $x\mapsto\sqrt{x}$; in other words, $\nu_a$ is the spectral measure of $|a|:=\sqrt{a^\ast a}$.

For $z\in\C$, define the {\bf log potential} $U_a\colon\C\to\R\cup\{-\infty\}$ by
\[ U_a(z):= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty \log(x)\,\nu_{a-z}(dx). \]
It is a subharmonic function, and so its (weak) Laplacian is a positive Radon measure.  In this case it is a probability measure: the {\bf Brown measure of $a$}
\[ \mu_a:= \Delta U_a \quad \text{i.e.} \quad
\int_{\C} \psi\,d\mu_a = \int_{\C} \Delta\psi(z)\, U_a(z)\,dz \qquad \forall\,\psi\in C^\infty(\C). \]
The Brown measure is then also uniquely defined by 
\[ \int_{\C} \log |\lambda-z|\,\mu_a(d\lambda) = U_a(z). \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.499458+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_4f46b2de22e7549670bcc1dce7b0f972c96bfd2b3336d5d4426cf06f59a598fa","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Weierstrass convergence theorem (a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic and derivatives converge locally uniformly) has no real-variable analogue and does not upgrade to uniform convergence on the whole domain. (1) Real failure: f_n(x) = sin(n^2 x)/n converges to 0 uniformly on R, but the derivatives f_n'(x) = n cos(n^2 x) do not converge to the derivative of the limit — at x = 0, f_n'(0) = n → ∞ — so uniform convergence of real functions carries no information about derivatives. More dramatically, by the Weierstrass approximation theorem every continuous nowhere differentiable function on [0,1] is a uniform limit of polynomials, so uniform limits of real-analytic functions need not be differentiable anywhere. The complex proof uses the Cauchy estimates, which need holomorphy on a two-dimensional neighborhood: a bound on |g| on a disk controls all derivatives at the center. (2) Only locally uniform: f_n(z) = z^n/n converges to 0 uniformly on all of D, yet f_n'(z) = z^{n-1} has supremum 1 on D for every n and does not converge uniformly on D. So the derivative statement must be quoted with 'uniformly on compact subsets'; deducing a uniform derivative bound up to the boundary from a uniform bound on the functions is a genuine error, and controlling it requires extra input (a larger domain of holomorphy, or boundary regularity). (3) The hypothesis is convergence on compact subsets of the open set, not convergence on the closed set: a sequence converging uniformly on the closed unit disk still gives derivative convergence only on |z| ≤ r < 1 unless the functions are holomorphic on a larger disk.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:25:39.116617+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_4f52df7591d276d237c39a099ff651be4172081a5ae7f970158d4c820b49a008","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def: partition procedure in sle of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Fix a sufficiently small constant $\iota>0$, and set
$M=\iota r^{3\kappa}N.$
For a box $\mathsf{B}$, write
$S_\gamma(\mathsf{B}):=\sum_{x\in\mathsf{B}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,\gamma)^{-1/4}.$
We define the following recursive partition procedure. We first partition $\Lambda_N$ into boxes of side length $M$. Given a current box $\mathsf{B}$, we proceed as follows.

If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4},
$
we leave $\mathsf{B}$ unchanged.
If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})\ge M^{7/4},
$
we divide $\mathsf{B}$ into two sub-boxes according to the following rule. Suppose, after translation and rotation if necessary, that
$
\mathsf{B}=[1,a]\times[1,b],
1\le a\le b.
$
For \(0\le c\le b\), let
$
\mathsf{C}_1(c)=[1,a]\times[1,c],
\mathsf{C}_2(c)=[1,a]\times[c+1,b],
$
with the convention that empty boxes are omitted. We choose \(c\) so that
$
\big|S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_1(c))-S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_2(c))\big|
$
is minimized, and replace \(\mathsf{B}\) by the two boxes \(\mathsf{C}_1(c)\) and \(\mathsf{C}_2(c)\).

We repeat this procedure until every current box \(\mathsf{B}\) satisfies
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4}.
$
The resulting collection of boxes is denoted by
$
\mathsf{B}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{B}_n.
$
Finally, we set
$
\mathsf{B}_i^+=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^+,
\mathsf{B}_i^-=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^-.
$","status":"unverified"}

The order of f is ρ = limsup_{r→∞} (log log M(r))/(log r) in [0, ∞]; equivalently ρ = inf{λ ≥ 0 : M(r) ≤ exp(r^λ) for all sufficiently large r}, with the infimum of the empty set taken to be ∞. Examples: every nonconstant polynomial has order 0; exp(z), sin z, cos z and 1/Γ have order 1; exp(z^n) has order n; cos(sqrt z) has order 1/2; exp(exp(z)) has infinite order. Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa}${} in a simply connected domain $D$, and let $\Upsilon_\Gamma$ be its gasket. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exists $p > 0$ such that the following holds.

There exists a resampling $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ be the event that $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ has a loop $\widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that
\begin{itemize}
 \item disconnects every point in $\Upsilon_{\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}} \cap B(z,2^{-j})$ from $\partial B(z,2^{-j+1})$,
 \item the gasket and the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$, let $\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k}$ be the event that the number of $j=j_0+1,\ldots,j_0+k$ so that
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j} \,|\, \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[(\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k})^c] = O(e^{-b k}) \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:49.563974+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5006309e62aea00056c601df1f4c1dc24277d7d7e5d5ce336b025a44cde269c6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 8 (Shared-scale uniform vs.\\ allocation-flexible) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] We contrast two settings by two freedoms they grant: to allocate bits across coordinates, and to give each coordinate its own scale. A quantizer is \\emph{shared-scale uniform} if every coefficient of a group is stored at the same bit-width on a uniform grid with a single shared scale, so no bits can be re-allocated between coordinates: the per-group \\texttt{INT4} grid of a deployed low-bit kernel (\\texttt{MXFP4} and \\texttt{NVFP4} are shared-scale on a \\emph{non-uniform} element grid, a second axis taken up in \\Cref{sec:format}). It is \\emph{allocation-flexible} if the coder may spend a different number of bits on different coordinates under a fixed \\emph{total}-rate budget: realized by unequal (but deterministic) bit assignment, by entropy coding of the indices, or both, as in a classical transform coder. \\textbf{Every deployed LLM GEMM kernel is shared-scale, fixed-allocation}, for the datapath reasons developed in \\Cref{sec:inversion}; the classical transform-coding theory of \\Cref{sec:classical} is allocation-flexible.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:48:17.126971+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_502ad83e7404b19f631ece643f03381dc34a5c721250602dcb68a2876455d6ab","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 15 ({\cite[p.\ 110) of arXiv:2605.27974, 'Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resista'] {FOT}}]
    Let $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ be a Dirichlet form on $L^2(X, \mu)$ and assume that 
    $\mathcal{F} \subset C(X)$ and that $\mathcal{F}$ is dense in 
    $(C(X),\norm{\cdot}_{\infty})$. Then, for any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, 
    there exists a unique finite Borel measure $\nu_{f}$ on $X$ which satisfies 
    \begin{align}
        \int_{X}g\,d\nu_{f}=2\mathcal{E}(fg,f)-\mathcal{E}(g,f^{2}), 
        \quad g \in \mathcal{F}.
    \end{align}
     The measure $\nu_{f}$ is called the energy measure of $f$. Also, for any 
     $f,g \in \mathcal{F}$, we define a signed measure $\nu_{f,g}$ by 
    \begin{equation}
        \nu_{f,g} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}(\nu_{f+g}-\nu_{f}-\nu_{g}).
    \end{equation}
    $\nu_{f,g}$ is called the mutual energy measure of $f$ and $g$. Then, we have 
    $\abs{\nu_{f,g}(B)} \leq \nu_{f}(B)^{1/2}\nu_{g}(B)^{1/2}$
    for any Borel set $B$ of $X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f ∈ C^1","u is a weak solution which is piecewise C^1 with C^1 shock curves and one-sided traces (the equivalence as stated is for this piecewise-smooth class; Kruzhkov's definition is what governs general L^∞ solutions)","the chord condition must hold at EVERY point of EVERY discontinuity curve","Rankine-Hugoniot alone is not sufficient: it fixes σ but permits inadmissible jumps"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T10:04:12.417666+00:00","domain":"partial differential equations: hyperbolic conservation laws","id":"claim_502c4a8cf7e11bf1fd64197cea9e23277293f004895262e4972b802ea4718867","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let f ∈ C^1(R) and let u ∈ L^∞(R × (0,∞)) be a weak solution of u_t + f(u)_x = 0 that is piecewise C^1: away from finitely many disjoint C^1 curves x = s_i(t) it is C^1, and it has C^1 one-sided traces u_-(t) (from x < s_i(t)) and u_+(t) (from x > s_i(t)) on each curve. Each curve then satisfies Rankine-Hugoniot, σ := s_i'(t) = ( f(u_-) - f(u_+) ) / ( u_- - u_+ ) when u_- ≠ u_+. Such a u is a Kruzhkov entropy solution if and only if at every point of every discontinuity curve the chord condition holds: for every k strictly between u_- and u_+, ( f(k) - f(u_-) ) / ( k - u_- ) ≥ σ ≥ ( f(k) - f(u_+) ) / ( k - u_+ ). Equivalently: if u_+ < u_-, the graph of f on [u_+,u_-] lies on or below the chord joining (u_+,f(u_+)) to (u_-,f(u_-)); if u_- < u_+, the graph of f on [u_-,u_+] lies on or above that chord. If f is strictly convex, this is equivalent to the Lax shock inequalities f'(u_-) ≥ σ ≥ f'(u_+), i.e. to u_- > u_+: a strictly convex flux admits only downward jumps.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.543870+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_503a791b1755d53c7385e64d56512fef661f8ac68a58a89821ec3caef72ecfb3","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 (Coordinate representation) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $G$ be a finite graph and $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.
    Define $\mu_{G,\beta}'$ as the probability measure on
    \[
        \tau:=(\alpha,\omega,\eta)\in [0,\tfrac\pi2]^V\times\{0,1\}^E\times\{0,1\}^E:=\Pi_G
    \]
    with density
    \begin{align}
        &
        \diff\mu_{G,\beta}'(\tau)
        \propto
        \textstyle
        \left(\prod_{u\in V}\diff\alpha_u\right)
        \\
        &
        \qquad\qquad
        \textstyle
        \cdot
        2^{k(\omega)}
        \left(
            \prod_{uv\in \omega}
                (1-\e^{-2\beta(\cos\alpha_u)(\cos\alpha_v)})
            \middle)\middle(
            \prod_{uv\not\in\omega}
                e^{-2\beta(\cos\alpha_u)(\cos\alpha_v)}
            \right)
            \\&
            \qquad\qquad
            \textstyle
            \cdot
            2^{k(\eta)}
            \left(
                \prod_{uv\in \eta}
                     (1-\e^{-2\beta(\sin\alpha_u)(\sin\alpha_v)})
                \middle)\middle(
                \prod_{uv\not\in\eta}
                    e^{-2\beta(\sin\alpha_u)(\sin\alpha_v)}
                \right).
    \end{align}
    Here $k(\rho)$ denotes the number of connected components of $(V,\rho)$.

    Now obtain a sample $\sigma\in(\S^1)^V$ as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Sample $\tau\sim\mu_{G,\beta}'$,
        \item Sample $\xi\in\{-1,+1\}^V$ by flipping a fair coin for each connected component of $\omega$,
        \item Sample $\zeta\in\{-1,+1\}^V$ by flipping a fair coin for each connected component of $\eta$,
        \item Set $\sigma_u:=\xi_u\cos\alpha_u + i\cdot \zeta_u\sin\alpha_u$ for each $u\in V$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then $\sigma\sim\mu_{G,\beta}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["bond percolation on the square lattice Z^2","the Harris half as sketched uses Burton-Keane uniqueness, self-duality, the square-root trick and a planar topological argument","the Kesten half is stated but not proved in this node"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543220+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5050896df8f7fb9dbfa990fc0b0cefbd0928a39e58de37c123d446e63228d84e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For bond percolation on the square lattice Z^2, p_c = 1/2, and moreover theta(1/2) = 0: there is no infinite open cluster AT the critical point. The two halves have separate histories and separate proofs. HARRIS (1960) proved theta(1/2) = 0, which gives p_c >= 1/2. KESTEN (1980) proved that theta(p) > 0 for every p > 1/2, giving p_c <= 1/2. The self-duality of Z^2 bond percolation at p = 1/2 - the dual of the open configuration at parameter p is a configuration at parameter 1 - p on an isomorphic lattice - makes 1/2 the ONLY candidate but does not by itself decide the critical behaviour, which is why the theorem is hard. The corresponding value for SITE percolation on Z^2 is not known; for site percolation on the triangular lattice the answer is 1/2 by the same duality mechanism, and that is the case where conformal invariance at criticality is proved. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T01:54:57.544734+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_505cff961fe29adc78b740b001ea81ac013720965efddfef7f16a6e13715fb7e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:conv-immig of arXiv:2412.03325, 'Functional limit theorem for branching processes \\ in nearly degenerate varying environme'] Assume that the BPVEI $(Y_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ defined in (equation eq:Y of the paper) satisfies the conditions (C1)--(C3) and (C4) or (C4') holds. Then, for any $0<\varepsilon \leq 1$,
\[
\mathcal{L} ((Y_{A(nt)})_{t \geq  \varepsilon}) 
\stackrel{\mathcal{D}}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{L} ((W(\log t))_{t \geq \varepsilon}),
\]
as $n\to \infty$, 
where $(W(u))_{u\geq \log \varepsilon}$ is a continuous time branching 
process with immigration with initial distribution having g.f.,
\[
\log f_Y(s) 
= 
\begin{cases}
-\sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} 
\frac{2^k\lambda_k}{\nu^k} \left( \log\left( 
1+\frac{\nu}{2}(1-s)\right) +
\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{\nu^i}{i2^i}
(s-1)^i\right), & \nu > 0, \\
\sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} \frac{\lambda_k}{k} (s-1)^k, & \nu = 0,
\end{cases}
\]
with parameters $\alpha = 1+\nu$, $\beta = \sum_{k=1}^{\kappa}(-1)^{k+1}\lambda_k$,
and
\[
\begin{split}
f(s) & = (1+\nu)^{-1} \left(1+\frac{\nu}{2} + \frac{\nu}{2}s^2\right), \\
h(s) & = 1 + \beta^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^{\kappa} \lambda_k (s-1)^k,
\end{split}
\]
offspring and immigration g.f.'s, where $\kappa=K-1$ or $\kappa=\infty$ depending on whether condition (C4) or (C4') holds. The transition generating function of $W$ is given by
\begin{equation*} 
G_y(s, t) = \mathbf{E} \left[ s^{W(t + u)} | W(u) = y \right] = 
\frac{f_Y(s)}{f_Y(h_{e^{-t}}(s))} \left( h_{e^{-t}}(s) \right)^y.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:53:30.651266+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_50652d2136ddb08dcb7ce5e74196e731756b45ad795be53c5b0a7bbeb1e83aec","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $j \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ and suppose $\mathcal{Z}$ is a positive solution to the system of PDEs, such that the limit

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:45:05.499357+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5077f94fe968a69b5524c97ed548fb227f432bb16e32a29c1f81cf965563b699","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] A tracial \(*\)-probability space is a unital \(*\)-algebra
\(\mathscr{A}\) over \(\C\), together with a linear functional
\(\varphi:\mathscr{A}\to\C\) satisfying
\[
 \varphi(\mathbf{1})=1,\qquad
 \varphi(a^*a)\geq0,\qquad
 \varphi(ab)=\varphi(ba)
 \quad (a,b\in\mathscr{A}).
\]
If \(\mathscr{A}\) is a unital \(C^*\)-algebra, we call
\((\mathscr{A},\varphi)\) a tracial \(C^*\)-probability space.
The elements of \(\mathscr{A}\) are noncommutative random variables, and
their joint \(*\)-distribution is the collection of all mixed moments
\(\varphi(R(a_1,\ldots,a_k,a_1^*,\ldots,a_k^*))\).
A sequence \((\mathbf{M}_N)\) converges almost surely in
\(*\)-distribution to an element \(\mathsf{m}\in\mathscr{A}\) if, for
every noncommutative polynomial \(R\) in two indeterminates,
\begin{equation}
 \tr_N R(\mathbf{M}_N,\mathbf{M}_N^*)
 \longrightarrow \varphi(R(\mathsf{m},\mathsf{m}^*))
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.343860+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_507d5ba3adbc2e429305407bf209c503f43913155e6b2add4cee1953b366b057","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Consider two matrices $M$ and $N$ of size $r \times r$ and $s \times s$ respectively, and call $M'$ the matrix obtained by removing the last row and column from $M$ and $N'$ the one obtained by removing the first row and column from $N$. Define also two rectangular matrices $X$ and $Y$ of rank 1 and size $s \times r$ and $r \times s$ respectively, whose entries are all $0$ except for $(X)_{1,r}=:x$ and $(Y)_{r,1}=:y$. Then if we define the $2 \times 2$ block matrix
\[ A = \begin{pmatrix}
M & Y \\
X & N
\end{pmatrix} \]
we have
\[ \det A  = \det M \det N - x y \det M' \det N' . \]
\begin{proof}
We prove the formula through the Laplace expansion of the determinant. For a matrix $T$, we denote by $\mu_{i,j}(T)$ the minor obtained by removing the $i$-th row and $j$-th column from $T$. Using Laplace expansion on the $r$-th row of $A$ we get
\[ \det A = \sum_{i=1}^{r+1} (-1)^{i+r} A_{r,i}~\mu_{r,i}(A)  . \]
Now we notice that $\mu_{r,i}(A) = \mu_{r,i}(M) \det N $ for $i \leq r$. Then we have
\[ \det A = \left( \sum_{i=1}^r (-1)^{i+r} M_{r,i}~\mu_{r,i}(M) \right) \det N + (-1)^{2r+1} y~\mu_{r,r+1}(A) = \det M \det N - y~\mu_{r,r+1}(A). \]
Then we observe that if we remove the $r$-th row and $r+1$-th column from $A$ we get the following block matrix:
\[ \begin{pmatrix}
M' & M^r & 0 \\
0 & x & N_1 \\
0 & 0 & N'
\end{pmatrix}, \]
where $M^r$ denotes the $r$-th column of $M$ without $M_{r,r}$ and $N_1$ denotes the first row of $N$ without $N_{1,1}$. It is then obvious to see that
\[ \mu_{r,r+1}(A) = x \det M' \det N', \]
and that concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\[

is finite, and hence
\[
(L\varphi)(x):=\sum_{y\neq x} q(x,y)\big(\varphi(y)-\varphi(x)\big)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:33:23.329702+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_50e99db7fab5de34e42901cf169a0e65c9872e5e8b323f985fe2bd615bfa0997","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 3 of arXiv:2506.21829, 'Some notes on Lamperti's recurrence of stochastic sequences'] Assume that \eqref{1}, integrability condition \eqref{2} and assumptions \eqref{4.3}, \eqref{4.4}, \eqref{4.5} and \eqref{4.6} are satisfied.
Then the stochastic sequence is recurrent if, as $x\to\infty$, we almost surely have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{p\mathsf{E}\{X_{n+1}-X_n~|~X_n=x, X_{n+1}>X_n, X_{n-1},\ldots, X_0\}}{q\mathsf{E}\{X_{n}-X_{n+1}~|~X_n=x, X_{n+1}<X_n, X_{n-1},\ldots, X_0\}}\\
&\leq1+\frac{R}{x}+O\left(\frac{1}{x^{1+\epsilon}}\right),
\end{aligned}
\]
where $R(x)=\mathsf{E}\{|X_{n+1}-X_n|~\big|~X_{n}=x, X_{n-1},\ldots, X_0\}$, and $R$ is the limit with probability $1$ of $R(x)$ as $x\to\infty$.
If instead
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{p\mathsf{E}\{X_{n+1}-X_n~|~X_n=x, X_{n+1}>X_n, X_{n-1},\ldots, X_0\}}{q\mathsf{E}\{X_{n}-X_{n+1}~|~X_n=x, X_{n+1}<X_n, X_{n-1},\ldots, X_0\}}\\
&\geq1+\frac{R\theta}{x},
\end{aligned}
\]
for some $\theta>1$ and almost all large $x$, then the stochastic sequence is transient.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:40:26.985133+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_50f38c297eb2a51d81d62b703abcf7d7dd19e114c846b528de2abe1a19dd0448","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:good-walk of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let~$G = (V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with degree bounded by~$d$ and satisfying the bound~(equation eq:return-bound of the paper) for some $d_s>0$ and $A<\infty$. Let $(\xi(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ and independent of the walk with $\mathbb{E}[\xi]\in(-\infty,0)$ and $\mathbb{E}[|\xi|^p]<\infty$ for some $p\geq 1$, and let $Y_k\coloneqq(\max_{2^k\leq n<2^{k+1}}W_n-|\mathbb{E}[\xi]|\,2^k/d)^+$. Let $\alpha\coloneqq(1-d_s/2)^+$ and fix $\delta\in(0,d_s/2\wedge 1)$. For $k\geq 0$, let
		\begin{equation}
			\mathcal{A}_k\coloneqq\bigl\{\max_v L_N(v)\leq N^{\alpha+\delta}\bigr\},\qquad N\coloneqq 2^{k+1}\,.
		\end{equation}
		Then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
			\item For every integer $r\geq 1$,
			\[
			\mathbb{P}_x(\mathcal{A}_k^c)\leq C_r\begin{cases}
				N^{d_s/2-r\delta} & \text{if } d_s<2,\\[3pt]
				N^{1-r\delta}(1{+}\log N)^{r-1} & \text{if } d_s=2,\\[3pt]
				N^{1-r\delta} & \text{if } d_s>2\,.
			\end{cases}\,
			\]
			\item $\mathbb{E}_x[Y_k^p]\leq C\,N^p$ uniformly in~$x$ and~$k$.
			\item For every $q\in[1,p)$ and $r$ large enough, $\mathbb{E}_x[Y_k^q\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{A}_k^c}]=O(2^{-3k})$ uniformly in~$x$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:20:33.748203+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5119aefa059987b20f12db27480d76d172e58a0c0cd4c4f5a4252aa1385c07b2","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 14 (Renewal--reward CLT) of arXiv:2607.28865, 'First-Passage Percolation on Spread-out line graphs: Microscopic Regime'] Let $\{(X_i,Y_i)\}_{i\ge1}$ be i.i.d.~with $X_i\in\dN$,
\begin{align*}
\E X_1=\mu\in(0,\infty),
\qquad
\E Y_1=\nu\in\dR,
\qquad
\E X_1^2+\E Y_1^2<\infty.
\end{align*}
Define
\begin{align*}
S_m:=\sum_{i=1}^m X_i,
\qquad
R_m:=\sum_{i=1}^m Y_i,
\qquad
N_t:=\max\{m\ge0:S_m\le t\},
\qquad
R(t):=R_{N_t}.
\end{align*}
Then, as $t\to\infty$,
\begin{align}
t^{-1/2}\cdot (R(t)-t\cdot {\nu}/{\mu})
\Longrightarrow
\N(0,\sigma^2),
\end{align}
where $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{\mu} \var\left(Y_1-\nu/{\mu}\cdot X_1\right)$.
Equivalently,
\begin{align}
t^{-1/2}\cdot (R(t)-\E R(t))
\Longrightarrow
\N(0,\sigma^2).
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.217380+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_513d5c498ebf769a03ce0e5c529fae00a7d5909ab64031e4b50e889343b84b51","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:RR of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] Fix $\theta \in (0,1)$ and let $T, K_1$ be as above.
For $a_0\in \mathbb{R},  t_0 \ge 0$, $(x,t) \in B(a_0, t_0)$ and $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$, define $H(x,\varepsilon,\delta):= [x-\sigma\varepsilon^{-1/4}\delta-(\delta \log \delta^{-1})^{1/2}, x-\sigma\varepsilon^{-1/4}\delta+(\delta \log \delta^{-1})^{1/2}]^c$, and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.494264+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_513e6ccde40e00de941c0461f711fe6f1ed11768f73c046cd05e56a56bce74a7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 21 (One-hive marginal of the  quadruply augmented double hive law) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:double-one-hive}
Assume \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar d>0\), and assume either \(\bar f>0\), or
\[
\bar f^2<0,
\qquad
\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2<0.
\]
Let \(p_{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the density on \(\mathbb D^4\) from
Lemma~\ref{lem:double-maxent}.  Put
\[
T=\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2.
\]
Define the geometric side lengths
\[
a^2=\frac{\bar a^2(T-\bar a^2)}{T},\qquad
b^2=\frac{\bar b^2(T-\bar b^2)}{T},
\]
\[
d^2=\frac{\bar d^2(T-\bar d^2)}{T},\qquad
f^2=\frac{\bar f^2(T-\bar f^2)}{T},
\]
and
\[
c_*^2=
\frac{(\bar a^2+\bar b^2)(\bar d^2+\bar f^2)}{T}.
\]
In the second case these quantities are still positive, since
\(\bar d^2+\bar f^2<-(\bar a^2+\bar b^2)\).
Let \(h_1\) denote the first hive, so that
\[
h_1\in H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu).
\]
Then the marginal law of \(h_1\) is
\[
\mathcal H_n(a,b,c_*).
\]
Similarly, the marginal law of the second hive is
\(\mathcal H_n(d,f,c_*)\); in the case \(\bar f^2<0\), this is understood
using the symmetry of the three boundary components to place the imaginary
raw parameter in the third slot of Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian1}.  Moreover,
\(c_*\) is the value of the glued side selected by Lemma~\ref{lem:doublehive}:
it maximizes
\[
x\mapsto
\frac{\Delta_{abx}^2}{abx}\frac{\Delta_{xdf}^2}{xdf}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:32:28.951525+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5140b104c7857699ac49fa7ee275e1d3743af8cefb0cac2125ba4ae0c4f38e3a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem_decode of arXiv:2608.15344, 'A Harris recurrent continuous-time Markov process without wide-sense regenerative structur'] There exists a Borel measurable function $c:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathcal{V}$ with the following property. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T02:04:49.445287+00:00","domain":"probability theory (vocabulary)","id":"claim_5144be3db9c2bd722a2097f1ed50b2d0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a reversible chain with eigenvalues $1=\\lambda_1>\\lambda_2\\ge\\dots\\ge\\lambda_n$, the spectral gap is $\\gamma=1-\\lambda_2$ and the absolute gap $\\gamma_*=1-\\max(|\\lambda_2|,|\\lambda_n|)$; $\\mathrm{Var}_\\pi(P^tf)\\le(1-\\gamma_*)^{2t}\\mathrm{Var}_\\pi(f)$ and the relaxation time is $t_{rel}=1/\\gamma_*$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:44:39.740203+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5145cdcb718a7e954dba35500bf47590c07e908abbc17dc9685e09b5603a1bf9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.29855, 'Growth of Simple Closed Geodesics in closed Hyperbolic $3$-Manifolds'] For every $0<\varepsilon<1$ there exist a finite set
$S\subset\Gamma^+$, an open spherical disk

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.506900+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_5154a985d3d28740fb513ec5129931cdf440cc21d2927b0f4d484adee801c427","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 (\cite{xia1996vector}) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] We say that $\Phi$ is a scaling function for a vector-valued multiresolution analysis $\{V_j\}_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}$ of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ if the sequence $\{V_j\}_{j\in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(VMRA\arabic*)}]

\item $\bigcap_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} V_j=\{0\}$ and $\bigcup_{j\in \mathbb{Z}} V_j$ is dense in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$.

\item $h\in V_j$ if and only if $h(\cdot-k)\in V_{j}$ for all $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}^d$.
\item The sequence $\{\Phi(\cdot-k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ is an orthonormal basis of $V_0$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:40.361265+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_52073d77451f55fd7de4416cfcd945b90af910ed963d276f3197a650d30047e7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 48 (Coalescent subtrees) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] For \(0\le j\le h^*\), define the collection of the coalescent subtrees at height \(j\) by
\[
\mathbf{T}_j=\mathbf{T}_j(n,h^*):=\big\{\mathscr{T}^n(v): v\in \cX_j\big\}.
\]
Each element of \(\mathbf{T}_j\) is a subtree rooted at a vertex at height \(j\) that admits at least one descendant at height \(h^*\). Note that \(|\mathbf{T}_j|=|\cX_j|=X_j\).

We then write \(\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_{|\mathbf{T}_j|}\) for a uniform random ordering of the elements of \(\mathbf{T}_j\). Concretely, conditionally on \(\mathscr{T}^n\), we first list the elements of \(\mathbf{T}_j\) according to the lexicographical order of their roots, denoted by \(\mathbf{T}_j^{(1)},\ldots,\mathbf{T}_j^{(|\mathbf{T}_j|)}\). Then we choose a permutation \(\pi\) uniformly at random from the symmetric group on \(|\mathbf{T}_j|\) elements, and define
\[
(\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_{|\mathbf{T}_j|})
:= (\mathbf{T}_j^{(\pi(1))},\ldots,\mathbf{T}_j^{(\pi(|\mathbf{T}_j|))}).
\]
Finally, we introduce the labeling map
\begin{align}
    \Lambda_j : \mathbf{T}_j \longrightarrow \{1,\ldots,|\mathbf{T}_j|\}, \qquad
\Lambda_j(\mathsf{T}_i) := i,
\end{align}
which assigns to each coalescent subtree its index in the random ordering.  
The random orderings (and hence the labeling maps \(\Lambda_j\)) are taken independently across different heights~\(j\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.096313+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_521d8b2552ac54fe398b53b3651e9496b3fe562d609da8d501e77cfd5cdd303b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:ricci-removal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $P_z$ be the rank-one projector onto a unit decomposable bivector and
$C_z=P_z-N^{-1}I_W$.  If $L_z=-2z_{\rm mat}^2$ is the orthogonal
projector onto the plane of $z$, put
\[
 B_z=\frac{L_z-(2/n)I_H}{n-2}.
\tag{2.6.2}
\]
Then the orthogonal curvature decomposition is
\[
 C_z=W_z+X_{B_z},\qquad W_z\in\mathcal W,
 \qquad X_B(u\wedge v)=Bu\wedge v+u\wedge Bv,
\tag{2.6.3}
\]
with no scalar or $\Lambda^4H$ summand, and
\[
 \|B_z\|_\mathrm{op}=\frac1n,\qquad
 \|B_z\|_F^2=\frac{2}{n(n-2)},\qquad
 \|X_B\|_2^2=(n-2)\|B\|_F^2,\qquad
 \|X_B\|_\mathrm{op}\le2\|B\|_\mathrm{op}.
\tag{2.6.4}
\]

In the cumulative moving frame the transported $B_z$ are reverse
martingale differences.  If $\mathfrak B_r$ is their sum, then
\[
 \mathbb E\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^2=\frac{2r}{n(n-2)},\qquad
 \mathbb E\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^4
 \le C\frac{r^2}{n^2(n-2)^2},
\tag{2.6.5}
\]
and, for fixed $c$, uniformly over $r\le cN$,
\[
 \max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_\mathrm{op}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{2.6.6}
\]
More quantitatively, for every fixed $L$ and $1\le p\le L\log n$,
\[
 \left(\mathbb E\max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_\mathrm{op}^p\right)^{1/p}
 \le C_{c,L}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{p+\log n}{n}}+\frac{p+\log n}{n}
 \right)=o(1).
\tag{2.6.6a}
\]
The same martingale satisfies the dimension-free Frobenius estimate
\[
 \left(\mathbb E\max_{r\le cN}\|\mathfrak B_r\|_F^p\right)^{1/p}
 \le C_c\sqrt p,
 \qquad 2\le p\le L\log n.
\tag{2.6.6b}
\]

Finally let $A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{a_i}$.  For traceless symmetric $B$
on $H$ and arbitrary $Z\in\operatorname{End}(W)$, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_i(B,Z)&=\{X_B,[A_i,Z]\}a_i,&
 U_i(B,Z)&=\{X_B,Z\}a_i,\\
 E_i(B,Z)&=\{X_{[a_i,B]},Z\}a_i,&
 \bar E(B,Z)&=N^{-1}\sum_iE_i(B,Z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.6.7}
\]
Put $\Psi(T)=\sum_jA_jTa_j$ and
$H_B(Z)=-N^{-1}X_B\Psi(Z)$.  Then the exact two-gradient decomposition is
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal R_i=A_iU_i-(E_i-\bar E)
 -\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j-H_B(Z)},
 \qquad
 \bar E=\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j+H_B(Z),\qquad V_j=X_BZa_j,
\tag{2.6.8}
\]
and its star-normalized square functions obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1N\sum_i\|U_i\|^2
 &\le\frac{4(n-2)}N\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_j\|V_j\|^2
 &\le\frac{n-2}N\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_i\|E_i-\bar E\|^2
 &\le\frac{64}{n-1}\|B\|_F^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2.6.9}
\]
The residue obeys
\[
 \|H_B(Z)\|
 \le\frac{2\sqrt{n-2}}N\|B\|_\mathrm{op}\|Z\|_2.
\tag{2.6.9a}
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:47:40.720863+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_52493dc681fcbf3c8d03628c9857eb4046736aa952c18fea626b7f8542bed7ae","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Ideal gap of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] A sequence of proper lines $\eta_i$ in $Z$ which are the convex hulls of 
$\lbrace e_i^L,e_i^R\rbrace$ for a sequence of nested intervals 
$[e_i^L,e_i^R]$ in $\mathcal E$ is said to be {\em end nested}.

A point $p\in Z$ together with an end nested sequence $\eta_i$ as above for which
$\bigcap_i [e_i^L,e_i^R]$ is empty and for which $p \in \bigcap_i \eta_i$ is
called an {\em ideal gap}. We define an equivalence relation on ideal
gaps as follows. Let $S$ and $S'$ be a pair of sequences of nested intervals
in $\mathcal E$ with empty intersection. We say $S$ refines $S'$ if $S'$ is a subsequence
of $S$. The relation of refinement is not an equivalence relation,
but it generates an equivalence relation on sequences of nested intervals
in $\mathcal E$ with empty intersection by
$S {\originalsim} S'$ if there is a finite sequence $S=S_0,S_1,\cdots,S_n=S'$ 
so that for each $i$ either $S_i$ refines $S_{i+1}$ or $S_{i+1}$ refines $S_i$.
Say that two ideal gaps are equivalent if their associated
sequences of nested intervals are related by this equivalence relation.

A point $p$ as above is said to lie in the {\em support} of the 
equivalence class of the given ideal gap.","status":"unverified"}
