{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.787117+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_836d497c21908aba348057d5ceb1155c4a86698d982df544e31f675f77298324","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 5 (Conical complex) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] Let $(X,d)$ be an NPC space and let $O_X \in X$. \[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:13:31.916892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8371d8676913d6956e340c3ef74fadf4613300bfc6a107f30d0e717240100261","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:KW of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Lambda$ be a finite cubical subcomplex of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $\mathbb{G}$ a finite abelian group, $1\leq k\leq d$, $(J_{\mathbf{c}})_{\mathbf{c}\in \Lambda^{*,k}}$ be positive coupling constants and $h:\mathbb{G}\to \mathbb{R}$ be even.      $$
     \rho[\eta]\propto \prod_{\mathbf{c}\in {\Lambda_{d-k}}}\exp(J_{\mathbf{c}} h(\eta_{\mathfrak{c}})), \;\forall \eta\in \Omega, \qquad \gamma[\sigma]\propto 1,\;\forall\sigma\in\Sigma.
     $$
     Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper),

For each $\sigma \in\Sigma$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \sigma] = \delta_{(d^k(\sigma))^*}$, the Dirac measure on the dual of the co-boundary of $\sigma$ corresponding to taking the domain walls of the spin configuration.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.904699+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8374c7b57703b981a0eb69503356340ab30b6c11c70146ddff8d3063533aa779","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Conjecture of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] For each $d \ge 2$ and each $1 \le k \le d - 1$, there exists $0 < \lambda_{c,k}<\infty$

    \mathcal{C} = VC_r(X^n)$
    be the associated Vietoris-Rips complex

    Then, if $ \lambda > \lambda_{c,k}$, then
    \[

    as $r \to 0$,

        \[

Then there exists a natural equivalence ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}^{\circ}[-]\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\Phi_G(-)(\textup{id}_G)$ of functors $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\Spc$, where $\Phi_G\colon{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}\to\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})$ is obtained from the unique equivalence $\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul\Spc_\textup{Glo}$ by evaluating at $\mathbb B{G}$.

        If we continue to view $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ as an \emph{unenriched} category, the cocartesian unstraightening of the 1-functor $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\textbf{\textup{Cat}}\hookrightarrow\Cat_\infty,X\mapsto \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_{/X}$ is given by $\Ar(\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top})$. {"assumptions":["f in L^1(R^d) for the weak (1,1) bound; f in L^p for the strong bound","Lebesgue measure on R^d (the doubling property of the measure is what the proof uses)"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751428+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis","id":"claim_83dc1a42b76b6de69325a6175207b7e1669093bf0f53df5985f5dc3e5cdce959","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f in L^1_loc(R^d) define the centred maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r > 0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy. Then M is of WEAK type (1,1): for every f in L^1(R^d) and every lambda > 0, |{x : Mf(x) > lambda}| <= 3^d ||f||_1 / lambda. For 1 < p <= infinity, M is bounded on L^p: ||Mf||_p <= C(d,p) ||f||_p, with C(d,p) blowing up like p/(p-1) as p decreases to 1. M is NOT bounded on L^1: if f is not almost everywhere zero then Mf(x) >= c_d ||f||_1 / |x|^d for |x| large, which is not integrable, so Mf is in L^1 only when f = 0 a.e. The uncentred maximal function (supremum over all balls containing x) is comparable to the centred one, with constants depending only on d. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Theorem 1.1 and Chapter 3]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X takes values in a finite set of size m","X_hat is a function of Y alone, so X -> Y -> X_hat is a Markov chain","P_e = Pr(X_hat != X)"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236127+00:00","domain":"information theory","id":"claim_83dc491008b3e031d0e3a0ac5475fb48986b2f077baf5876dcd333a684d89f6b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a discrete random variable taking values in a finite set of size m, let Y be any random variable jointly distributed with X, and let X_hat = g(Y) be any estimator of X computed from Y alone, so that X -> Y -> X_hat forms a Markov chain. Let P_e = Pr(X_hat != X) be the error probability. Then H(X|Y) <= H_b(P_e) + P_e * log(m-1), where H_b(p) = -p*log p - (1-p)*log(1-p) is the binary entropy function. Consequently, if the conditional entropy H(X|Y) is bounded away from 0, the error probability P_e cannot be made arbitrarily small.","status":"unverified"}

    \begin{proof}
        It is clear that the forgetful functor admits a pointwise left adjoint (given by coproduct with the terminal object), and the Beck--Chevalley condition follows from fiberwise cocompleteness.

        \[
            {\mathcal{C}}(X)_{1/}\xrightarrow{\;f_!\;}{\mathcal{C}}(Y)_{f_!1/}\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon_!\;}{\mathcal{C}}(Y)_{1/}.
        \]
        To verify the Beck--Chevalley condition, consider a pullback
        \[

                A\arrow[r,"t"'] & B
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        in $\PSh(T)$ with $s\in\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}(B)$. Then the Beck--Chevalley map $s'_!t'^*\to t^*s_!$ is a natural transformation of cocontinuous functors ${\mathcal{C}}(B')\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$; we may therefore check invertibility after applying the equivalence from the previous proposition, i.e.\ after precomposing with $(-)_+\colon{\mathcal{C}}(B)\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$. However, as Beck--Chevalley maps compose, this fits into a commutative diagram
        \[

                t^*s_!(-)_+\arrow[r,"t^*\textup{BC}_!"'] & t^*(-)_+s_!\arrow[r,"\sim"'] & (-)_+t^*s_!\rlap,
            \end{tikzcd}

{"assumptions":["Real Lebesgue density p supported on a finite interval; p>=m>0 almost everywhere","Mean zero and variance one; no continuity, derivative or upper density bound assumed","For the matrix corollary: fixed independent iid real factor laws, Gaussian observation noise, N,P>=2,M>=1, positive finite aspect limits"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:16:22.797292+00:00","domain":"probability; Stein kernels; Gaussian matrix channels","id":"claim_83f6a1f11daf0b73d42501d7da22edf147524c35169a2125815646401fbaafd6","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own work, proof (unaudited); standard-form construction, novelty unestablished.

p(x)>=m>0 for almost every x in that interval. Assume E u=0,
E u^2=1. No continuity, differentiability, or upper bound on p is
assumed. Define, almost everywhere on its support,

 tau(x)=[integral_x^b y*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 eta(x)=[integral_x^b (y^2-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 zeta(x)=[integral_x^b (tau(y)-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x).       (1)

Then, for every bounded C1 h with bounded derivative,

 E[u*h(u)]=E[tau(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(u^2-1)*h(u)]=E[eta(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(tau(u)-1)*h(u)]=E[zeta(u)*h'(u)],               (2)

and the explicit bounds are

 0<=tau<=1/m, E tau=1,
 |eta|<=2/m, |zeta|<=2/m.                           (3)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:36:12.177577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84005a70176ace5fabd3383c9436c04a93fc7c065d2fbc235871053976c83d35","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 106 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$, and $x = \sum_{k\in K}f(k)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Let $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) + g(k)) = x + \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \item[(ii)] Let $\mf B$ be an HTM and $\varphi\colon\mf A\to\mf B$ be a continuous homomorphism. Then $\sum_{k\in K} \varphi(f(k)) = \varphi(x)$.   
  \item [(iii)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(-f(k)) = -x$.
  \item [(iv)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG and $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) - g(k)) = x - \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["iid edge weights in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<infinity","Fixed distinct endpoints in Z^2 and measurable canonical topmost geodesic selection","Deterministic edge partition; independent same-law block redraws and independent uniform reveal labels"],"created_at":"2026-10-07T04:14:29.906219+00:00","domain":"probability/first-passage-percolation","id":"claim_8410cbafacdae75cb85f1a69ed227c34","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider bond first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid edge weights supported in [a,b], where 0<a<=b<infinity, and fixed distinct vertices u,v. Let X=T(u,v) and choose a measurable canonical topmost minimizing geodesic (atoms and ties are allowed). Partition the edges into deterministic blocks Lambda. For each block independently redraw its weights from the original law, independently of the environment, and write X^Lambda for the passage time with only that block replaced. Let U_Lambda be the event that the original chosen geodesic uses an edge in Lambda. Give the blocks iid Uniform[0,1] labels tau_Lambda independent of all original and redrawn weights. F_t reveals each labeled block and its original/redrawn weight pair when tau_Lambda<=t; equivalently, for the probabilities of U_Lambda one may reveal only original weights. Define A2=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda (X^Lambda-X)^2], A2plus=sum_Lambda E[((X^Lambda-X)^+)^2], A4=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda ((X^Lambda-X)^+)^4], and Pbar(kappa)=sum_Lambda E[P(U_Lambda|F_(1-kappa))^2]. For every 0<kappa<1, Var(X)<=kappa A2plus+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa))<=kappa A2+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa)). Positivity and boundedness localize all relevant paths to a deterministic finite edge set, so only finitely many blocks contribute. The proof needs independent blocks, off-geodesic monotonicity and conditional expectations; isotropy and FKG are not assumptions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236543+00:00","domain":"numerical analysis","id":"claim_8448b322d9af94267599948f7ac8e35e7642de9c07050163cb44f14c3c789388","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"An explicit s-stage Runge-Kutta method for the initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t_0) = y_0, advances y_n to y_{n+1} = y_n + h * sum_{i=1}^{s} b_i * k_i, where k_i = f( t_n + c_i*h, y_n + h*sum_{j<i} a_{ij}*k_j ), and the coefficients a_{ij}, b_i, c_i (the Butcher tableau) typically satisfy c_i = sum_{j<i} a_{ij}. The method has order p if, for sufficiently smooth f, its Taylor expansion in h agrees with the Taylor expansion of the exact solution through the h^p term (equivalently, the local truncation error is O(h^{p+1})). Matching these Taylor expansions imposes polynomial equations on (a_{ij}, b_i, c_i) called order conditions: for example, order 1 requires sum_i b_i = 1, and order 2 additionally requires sum_i b_i*c_i = 1/2. In Butcher's rooted-tree theory there is one order condition per rooted tree up to order p, and the number of independent conditions grows faster than the number of stages s, which is why, for instance, no explicit Runge-Kutta method can reach an order equal to its stage count once the order exceeds 4.","status":"unverified"}

(Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j) exactly when Lambda(a) < 0 for every a; if Lambda(a) >= 0 for some a the maximum is attained and there are finitely many records (Lambda(1) = log pi_1 + log(1/(lambda-nu)) + 1 is positive once lambda - nu < e pi_1). Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. {"assumptions":["the group is the two-element Cayley group; the claim is a counterexample, not a general theorem","relaxation time is 1/(1 - lambda_2), the standard spectral-gap convention","the target is the geometric-time law of the base walk at tilt p"],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869264+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_8494f2b7e60391b8ead2ab87b96e7454cadc38307316484de8264628972059fc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: author_checked_limited_argument - a first-pass structural calculation; no independent review, prior art unverified, and the other questions in the source are untouched] For Metropolis chains targeting a geometric-time law on a Cayley group, the source asks whether the relaxation time decreases monotonically in the tilt p. CLAIM: NO, and the counterexample is the smallest possible one - the two-element group - with relaxation defined the standard way as 1/(1 - lambda_2). (i) NONLAZY BASE. The base walk flips the two states; the target is mu_p = (1/(2-p), (1-p)/(2-p)); the Metropolis matrix is [[p, 1-p],[1, 0]], whose second eigenvalue is p - 1, so tau(p) = 1/(2 - p), STRICTLY INCREASING in p. (ii) LAZY BASE, which removes the convention ambiguity because its spectrum is nonnegative. The base matrix has all entries 1/2, mu_p = ((1+p)/2, (1-p)/2), the Metropolis off-diagonal rates are (1-p)/(2(1+p)) and 1/2, and tau(p) = 1 + p, again increasing. (iii) If laziness is imposed AFTER forming the nonlazy Metropolis kernel, tau(p) = 2/(2 - p), still increasing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it refutes the literal monotonicity direction only. It does not answer the source's other universal-bound questions and does not resolve its undefined tau(infinity). CONVENTION CAVEAT recorded with the result: if 'relaxation' meant the inverse absolute spectral gap of a nonlazy chain, that convention differs - the lazy example exists precisely to remove the ambiguity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Normalized random-walk rho","Infinite connected d-regular Cayley graph","Sufficient criterion, not equivalence"],"created_at":"2026-10-10T09:11:38.048103+00:00","domain":"Bernoulli bond percolation on graphs","id":"claim_84a5edcb56cb3e3ab5affe7a2fef6535bd7b550c252ea1c6a2dfcdf5fcf9bcaf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"DRAFT source-backed correction, pending referee check. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.341853+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84cfc224db6b7fa396ea49448e46983d599563f717df849a5b991424184b2ed1","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Local split--merge--rewire rule) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(\omega\) be a configuration, let \(\cL(\omega)\) be the associated loop
configuration, let \(e=\{x,y\}\in E\), and let \(s\in S^1\setminus T(\omega)\) be a
regular time. Consider the effect of inserting at \((e,s)\) either a cross or a bar.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item If \(I_{\neq}(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting either a cross or a bar
    merges the two loops containing \((x,s)\) and \((y,s)\) into one.

    \item If \(I_+(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting a cross splits the loop into two,
    whereas inserting a bar rewires the loop without changing the number of loops.

    \item If \(I_-(\omega;e,s)=1\), then inserting a bar splits the loop into two,
    whereas inserting a cross rewires the loop without changing the number of loops.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:25:41.653524+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84d1c0bff6ee2928c1b5d7c1f22c961f42beb26b566f731a372a479b154b39f9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:Levy-stable-graph-approximation of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r)$ be a regular based loop family. A \emph{stable graph approximation} of $L$ is the data of a sequence of embedded topological maps $({\mathbb{G}}_n)_{n\geq1}$, and a sequence of graph-loop families
\[
 L_n=(\ell_{1,n},\ldots,\ell_{r,n}),
 \qquad
 \ell_{i,n}\in L_o({\mathbb{G}}_n),
\]
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathrm{mesh}}({\mathbb{G}}_n)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0$;
\item for every $i=1,\dots,r$,
\[
 d_1(\ell_{i,n},\ell_i)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0;
\]
\item for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a homeomorphism $h_n$ such that $L_n$ and $L$ have the same marked ambient ribbon type; and if $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ are the connected components of $\Sigma\setminus\Gamma(L)$ and
\[
 C_{j,n}:=h_n(C_j),
\]
then
\[
 |C_{j,n}|\longrightarrow|C_j|,
 \qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\]
\end{enumerate}
We say that $L$ has a stable graph approximation carried by the sequence $(\mathbb{G}_n)$.
The same notation is used for the corresponding cut-open compact surfaces with boundary.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:51:11.462278+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_84df8febc302453700a3fd9a719c80d22356b02eaba6257700137fb2c717841f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 12 ({\cite[Definition~2.26) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {BST}}]
The multiplier module $\J(\omega_X,\Gamma)$ is defined as
\[ \J(\omega_X,\Gamma):=\bigcap_{\pi:Y\rightarrow X} \Image ({\Tr}_{\pi}:\pi_{*}{\omega}_{Y}(-\lfloor \pi^{*}\Gamma \rfloor) \hookrightarrow {\omega}_{X}(- \lfloor\Gamma\rfloor)),\]
where $\pi$ runs through all proper birational morphisms $Y\rightarrow X$ with $Y$ normal.
For a log $\Q$-Gorenstein pair $(X,\Delta)$, the multiplier ideal $\J(X,\Delta)$ is defined by
\[ \J(X,\Delta):=\J(\omega_X, K_X +\Delta), \]
where $K_X$ is a canonical divisor associated with ${\omega}_{X}$. Since the choice of $K_X$ determines the inclusion ${\omega}_{X}\subset K(X)$, the multiplier ideal $\J(X,\Delta)$ can be regarded as an ideal of $\sO_X$. Note that the resulting ideal $\J(X,\Delta)\subset\sO_X$ is independent of the choice of $K_X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.353526+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_852b0d4dc9f07b4a7615f1f6a29dbffaeb09c786792fcf84fedbb2a651fa5708","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 204 (spatial rerandomization for spherical perceptron) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We use the buckets from Definition~\ref{d:buckets} to
 define a new process $\vY\equiv\vY^{\RomI:\RomIII}$, as follows. First let $a(q_0)$ be sampled uniformly at random from $[M]$. Then, conditional on $a(q_0), \ldots, a(q_d)$, we let $a(q_{d+1})$ be sampled from the measure $\bP$ conditional on the bucket at time $q_d$, that is,
    \[a(q_{d+1})
    \sim \bP
    \bigg( a = \cdot \,\bigg|\, 
    a\in B(q_d,a(q_d)) \bigg)\,.
    \]
We then let $\vY(q_d)$ be the average of $\vX^\trunc$ over all the particles in the bucket containing $a(q_d)$, 
    \beq
    \vY(q_d)
    =
    \sum_{a\in B(q_d,a(q_d))}
    \frac{\vX^\trunc(q_d,a)}{|B(q_d,a(q_d))|}
    \,.
    \eeq
Informally, $\vY$ is the process $\vX^\trunc$ with ``spatial rerandomization at scale $\eta$.'' It is easy to check (by induction) that each $a(q_d)$ is marginally uniform on $[M]$, which implies that $\vX^\trunc(q_d)$ and $\vY(q_d)$ are within $W_{\infty}$ distance $O(\eta/\delta)$ for each fixed $d$.  Likewise, we define $\vY^\frozen\equiv\vY^{\frozen,\RomI:\RomIII}$ to be the spatial rerandomization of $\vX^\frozen$ at scale $\eta$, with random indices $a^\frozen(q_d) \in[M^\frozen]$
and buckets $\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)$.","status":"unverified"}
